definitions.name: Collaboration.collaborationRole
descriptions: Represents the participants in the Collaboration.

definitions.name: Collaboration
descriptions: A Collaboration describes a structure of collaborating elements (roles), each performing a specialized function, which collectively accomplish some desired functionality.

definitions.name: CollaborationUse.client_elements
descriptions: All the client elements of a roleBinding are in one Classifier and all supplier elements of a roleBinding are in one Collaboration.

expressions.body:
roleBinding->collect(client)->forAll(ne1, ne2 |
  ne1.oclIsKindOf(ConnectableElement) and ne2.oclIsKindOf(ConnectableElement) and
    let ce1 : ConnectableElement = ne1.oclAsType(ConnectableElement), ce2 : ConnectableElement = ne2.oclAsType(ConnectableElement) in
      ce1.structuredClassifier = ce2.structuredClassifier)
and
  roleBinding->collect(supplier)->forAll(ne1, ne2 |
  ne1.oclIsKindOf(ConnectableElement) and ne2.oclIsKindOf(ConnectableElement) and
    let ce1 : ConnectableElement = ne1.oclAsType(ConnectableElement), ce2 : ConnectableElement = ne2.oclAsType(ConnectableElement) in
      ce1.collaboration = ce2.collaboration)

definitions.name: CollaborationUse.every_role
descriptions: Every collaborationRole in the Collaboration is bound within the CollaborationUse.

definitions.name: CollaborationUse.connectors
descriptions: Connectors in a Collaboration typing a CollaborationUse must have corresponding Connectors between elements bound in the context Classifier, and these corresponding Connectors must have the same or more general type than the Collaboration Connectors.

expressions.body:
type.ownedConnector->forAll(connector |
  let rolesConnectedInCollab : Set(ConnectableElement) = connector.end.role->asSet(),
        relevantBindings : Set(Dependency) = roleBinding->select(rb | rb.supplier->intersection(rolesConnectedInCollab)->notEmpty()),
        boundRoles : Set(ConnectableElement) = relevantBindings->collect(client.oclAsType(ConnectableElement))->asSet(),
        contextClassifier : StructuredClassifier = boundRoles->any(true).structuredClassifier->any(true) in
          contextClassifier.ownedConnector->exists( correspondingConnector | 
              correspondingConnector.end.role->forAll( role | boundRoles->includes(role) )
              and (connector.type->notEmpty() and correspondingConnector.type->notEmpty()) implies connector.type->forAll(conformsTo(correspondingConnector.type)) )
)

definitions.limitation: The XMI chooses an arbitrary structuredClassifier association end. Python prefers the owning CollaborationUse classifier when represented, otherwise requires one shared context; ambiguous unowned uses remain unsupported.

definitions.name: CollaborationUse.roleBinding
descriptions: A mapping between features of the Collaboration and features of the owning Classifier. This mapping indicates which ConnectableElement of the Classifier plays which role(s) in the Collaboration. A ConnectableElement may be bound to multiple roles in the same CollaborationUse (that is, it may play multiple roles).

definitions.name: CollaborationUse.type
descriptions: The Collaboration which is used in this CollaborationUse. The Collaboration defines the cooperation between its roles which are mapped to ConnectableElements relating to the Classifier owning the CollaborationUse.

definitions.name: CollaborationUse
descriptions: A CollaborationUse is used to specify the application of a pattern specified by a Collaboration to a specific situation.

definitions.name: Component.provided
descriptions: Derivation for Component::/provided

expressions.body:
result = (let 	ris : Set(Interface) = allRealizedInterfaces(),
        realizingClassifiers : Set(Classifier) =  self.realization.realizingClassifier->union(self.allParents()->collect(realization.realizingClassifier))->asSet(),
        allRealizingClassifiers : Set(Classifier) = realizingClassifiers->union(realizingClassifiers.allParents())->asSet(),
        realizingClassifierInterfaces : Set(Interface) = allRealizingClassifiers->iterate(c; rci : Set(Interface) = Set{} | rci->union(c.allRealizedInterfaces())),
        ports : Set(Port) = self.ownedPort->union(allParents()->collect(ownedPort))->asSet(),
        providedByPorts : Set(Interface) = ports.provided->asSet()
in     ris->union(realizingClassifierInterfaces) ->union(providedByPorts)->asSet())

definitions.name: Component.required
descriptions: Derivation for Component::/required

expressions.body:
result = (let 	uis : Set(Interface) = allUsedInterfaces(),
        realizingClassifiers : Set(Classifier) = self.realization.realizingClassifier->union(self.allParents()->collect(realization.realizingClassifier))->asSet(),
        allRealizingClassifiers : Set(Classifier) = realizingClassifiers->union(realizingClassifiers.allParents())->asSet(),
        realizingClassifierInterfaces : Set(Interface) = allRealizingClassifiers->iterate(c; rci : Set(Interface) = Set{} | rci->union(c.allUsedInterfaces())),
        ports : Set(Port) = self.ownedPort->union(allParents()->collect(ownedPort))->asSet(),
        usedByPorts : Set(Interface) = ports.required->asSet()
in	    uis->union(realizingClassifierInterfaces)->union(usedByPorts)->asSet()
)

definitions.name: Component.no_nested_classifiers
descriptions: A Component cannot nest Classifiers.

definitions.name: Component.no_packaged_elements
descriptions: A Component nested in a Class cannot have any packaged elements.

definitions.name: Component.isIndirectlyInstantiated
descriptions: If true, the Component is defined at design-time, but at run-time (or execution-time) an object specified by the Component does not exist, that is, the Component is instantiated indirectly, through the instantiation of its realizing Classifiers or parts.

definitions.name: Component.packagedElement
descriptions: The set of PackageableElements that a Component owns. In the namespace of a Component, all model elements that are involved in or related to its definition may be owned or imported explicitly. These may include e.g., Classes, Interfaces, Components, Packages, UseCases, Dependencies (e.g., mappings), and Artifacts.

definitions.name: Component.provided
descriptions: The Interfaces that the Component exposes to its environment. These Interfaces may be Realized by the Component or any of its realizingClassifiers, or they may be the Interfaces that are provided by its public Ports.

definitions.name: Component.realization
descriptions: The set of Realizations owned by the Component. Realizations reference the Classifiers of which the Component is an abstraction; i.e., that realize its behavior.

definitions.name: Component.required
descriptions: The Interfaces that the Component requires from other Components in its environment in order to be able to offer its full set of provided functionality. These Interfaces may be used by the Component or any of its realizingClassifiers, or they may be the Interfaces that are required by its public Ports.

definitions.name: Component
descriptions: A Component represents a modular part of a system that encapsulates its contents and whose manifestation is replaceable within its environment.

definitions.name: ComponentRealization.abstraction
descriptions: The Component that owns this ComponentRealization and which is implemented by its realizing Classifiers.

definitions.name: ComponentRealization.realizingClassifier
descriptions: The Classifiers that are involved in the implementation of the Component that owns this Realization.

definitions.name: ComponentRealization
descriptions: Realization is specialized to (optionally) define the Classifiers that realize the contract offered by a Component in terms of its provided and required Interfaces. The Component forms an abstraction from these various Classifiers.

definitions.name: ConnectableElement.end
descriptions: Derivation for ConnectableElement::/end : ConnectorEnd

definitions.name: ConnectableElement.end
descriptions: A set of ConnectorEnds that attach to this ConnectableElement.

definitions.name: ConnectableElement.templateParameter
descriptions: The ConnectableElementTemplateParameter for this ConnectableElement parameter.

definitions.name: ConnectableElement
descriptions: ConnectableElement is an abstract metaclass representing a set of instances that play roles of a StructuredClassifier. ConnectableElements may be joined by attached Connectors and specify configurations of linked instances to be created within an instance of the containing StructuredClassifier.

definitions.name: ConnectableElementTemplateParameter.parameteredElement
descriptions: The ConnectableElement for this ConnectableElementTemplateParameter.

definitions.name: ConnectableElementTemplateParameter
descriptions: A ConnectableElementTemplateParameter exposes a ConnectableElement as a formal parameter for a template.

definitions.name: Connector.kind
descriptions: Derivation for Connector::/kind : ConnectorKind

expressions.body:
result = (if end->exists(
		role.oclIsKindOf(Port) 
		and partWithPort->isEmpty()
		and not role.oclAsType(Port).isBehavior)
then ConnectorKind::delegation 
else ConnectorKind::assembly 
endif)

definitions.name: Connector.types
descriptions: The types of the ConnectableElements that the ends of a Connector are attached to must conform to the types of the ends of the Association that types the Connector, if any.

expressions.body:
type<>null implies 
  let noOfEnds : Integer = end->size() in 
  (type.memberEnd->size() = noOfEnds) and Sequence{1..noOfEnds}->forAll(i | end->at(i).role.type.conformsTo(type.memberEnd->at(i).type))

definitions.name: Connector.roles
descriptions: The ConnectableElements attached as roles to each ConnectorEnd owned by a Connector must be owned or inherited roles of the Classifier that owned the Connector, or they must be Ports of such roles.

expressions.body:
structuredClassifier <> null
and
  end->forAll( e | structuredClassifier.allRoles()->includes(e.role)
or
  e.role.oclIsKindOf(Port) and structuredClassifier.allRoles()->includes(e.partWithPort))

definitions.name: Connector.contract
descriptions: The set of Behaviors that specify the valid interaction patterns across the Connector.

definitions.name: Connector.end
descriptions: A Connector has at least two ConnectorEnds, each representing the participation of instances of the Classifiers typing the ConnectableElements attached to the end. The set of ConnectorEnds is ordered.

definitions.name: Connector.kind
descriptions: Indicates the kind of Connector. This is derived: a Connector with one or more ends connected to a Port which is not on a Part and which is not a behavior port is a delegation; otherwise it is an assembly.

definitions.name: Connector.redefinedConnector
descriptions: A Connector may be redefined when its containing Classifier is specialized. The redefining Connector may have a type that specializes the type of the redefined Connector. The types of the ConnectorEnds of the redefining Connector may specialize the types of the ConnectorEnds of the redefined Connector. The properties of the ConnectorEnds of the redefining Connector may be replaced.

definitions.name: Connector.type
descriptions: An optional Association that classifies links corresponding to this Connector.

definitions.name: Connector
descriptions: A Connector specifies links that enables communication between two or more instances. In contrast to Associations, which specify links between any instance of the associated Classifiers, Connectors specify links between instances playing the connected parts only.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.definingEnd
descriptions: Derivation for ConnectorEnd::/definingEnd : Property

expressions.body:
result = (if connector.type = null 
then
  null 
else
  let index : Integer = connector.end->indexOf(self) in
    connector.type.memberEnd->at(index)
endif)

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.role_and_part_with_port
descriptions: If a ConnectorEnd references a partWithPort, then the role must be a Port that is defined or inherited by the type of the partWithPort.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.part_with_port_empty
descriptions: If a ConnectorEnd is attached to a Port of the containing Classifier, partWithPort will be empty.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.multiplicity
descriptions: The multiplicity of the ConnectorEnd may not be more general than the multiplicity of the corresponding end of the Association typing the owning Connector, if any.
definitions.limitation: The unconditional formula passes an absent definingEnd to compatibleWith. Python follows the prose: an untyped connector has no association-end bound to constrain it.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.self_part_with_port
descriptions: The Property held in self.partWithPort must not be a Port.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.definingEnd
descriptions: A derived property referencing the corresponding end on the Association which types the Connector owing this ConnectorEnd, if any. It is derived by selecting the end at the same place in the ordering of Association ends as this ConnectorEnd.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.partWithPort
descriptions: Indicates the role of the internal structure of a Classifier with the Port to which the ConnectorEnd is attached.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd.role
descriptions: The ConnectableElement attached at this ConnectorEnd. When an instance of the containing Classifier is created, a link may (depending on the multiplicities) be created to an instance of the Classifier that types this ConnectableElement.

definitions.name: ConnectorEnd
descriptions: A ConnectorEnd is an endpoint of a Connector, which attaches the Connector to a ConnectableElement.

definitions.name: EncapsulatedClassifier.ownedPort
descriptions: Derivation for EncapsulatedClassifier::/ownedPort : Port

definitions.name: EncapsulatedClassifier.ownedPort
descriptions: The Ports owned by the EncapsulatedClassifier.

definitions.name: EncapsulatedClassifier
descriptions: An EncapsulatedClassifier may own Ports to specify typed interaction points.

definitions.name: Port.provided
descriptions: Derivation for Port::/provided

expressions.body: result = (if isConjugated then basicRequired() else basicProvided() endif)

definitions.name: Port.required
descriptions: Derivation for Port::/required

expressions.body: result = (if isConjugated then basicProvided() else basicRequired() endif)

definitions.name: Port.basicProvided
descriptions: The union of the sets of Interfaces realized by the type of the Port and its supertypes, or directly the type of the Port if the Port is typed by an Interface.

expressions.body:
result = (if type.oclIsKindOf(Interface) 
then type.oclAsType(Interface)->asSet() 
else type.oclAsType(Classifier).allRealizedInterfaces() 
endif)

definitions.name: Port.basicRequired
descriptions: The union of the sets of Interfaces used by the type of the Port and its supertypes.

definitions.name: Port.port_aggregation
descriptions: Port.aggregation must be composite.

definitions.name: Port.default_value
descriptions: A defaultValue for port cannot be specified when the type of the Port is an Interface.

definitions.name: Port.encapsulated_owner
descriptions: All Ports are owned by an EncapsulatedClassifier.
definitions.limitation: The null=null formula admits unowned ports. Python follows the ownership description and requires an EncapsulatedClassifier owner.

definitions.name: Port.isBehavior
descriptions: Specifies whether requests arriving at this Port are sent to the classifier behavior of this EncapsulatedClassifier. Such a Port is referred to as a behavior Port. Any invocation of a BehavioralFeature targeted at a behavior Port will be handled by the instance of the owning EncapsulatedClassifier itself, rather than by any instances that it may contain.

definitions.name: Port.isConjugated
descriptions: Specifies the way that the provided and required Interfaces are derived from the Port’s Type.

definitions.name: Port.isService
descriptions: If true, indicates that this Port is used to provide the published functionality of an EncapsulatedClassifier.  If false, this Port is used to implement the EncapsulatedClassifier but is not part of the essential externally-visible functionality of the EncapsulatedClassifier and can, therefore, be altered or deleted along with the internal implementation of the EncapsulatedClassifier and other properties that are considered part of its implementation.

definitions.name: Port.protocol
descriptions: An optional ProtocolStateMachine which describes valid interactions at this interaction point.

definitions.name: Port.provided
descriptions: The Interfaces specifying the set of Operations and Receptions that the EncapsulatedCclassifier offers to its environment via this Port, and which it will handle either directly or by forwarding it to a part of its internal structure. This association is derived according to the value of isConjugated. If isConjugated is false, provided is derived as the union of the sets of Interfaces realized by the type of the port and its supertypes, or directly from the type of the Port if the Port is typed by an Interface. If isConjugated is true, it is derived as the union of the sets of Interfaces used by the type of the Port and its supertypes.

definitions.name: Port.redefinedPort
descriptions: A Port may be redefined when its containing EncapsulatedClassifier is specialized. The redefining Port may have additional Interfaces to those that are associated with the redefined Port or it may replace an Interface by one of its subtypes.

definitions.name: Port.required
descriptions: The Interfaces specifying the set of Operations and Receptions that the EncapsulatedCassifier expects its environment to handle via this port. This association is derived according to the value of isConjugated. If isConjugated is false, required is derived as the union of the sets of Interfaces used by the type of the Port and its supertypes. If isConjugated is true, it is derived as the union of the sets of Interfaces realized by the type of the Port and its supertypes, or directly from the type of the Port if the Port is typed by an Interface.

definitions.name: Port
descriptions: A Port is a property of an EncapsulatedClassifier that specifies a distinct interaction point between that EncapsulatedClassifier and its environment or between the (behavior of the) EncapsulatedClassifier and its internal parts. Ports are connected to Properties of the EncapsulatedClassifier by Connectors through which requests can be made to invoke BehavioralFeatures. A Port may specify the services an EncapsulatedClassifier provides (offers) to its environment as well as the services that an EncapsulatedClassifier expects (requires) of its environment.  A Port may have an associated ProtocolStateMachine.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.part
descriptions: Derivation for StructuredClassifier::/part

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.allRoles
descriptions: All features of type ConnectableElement, equivalent to all direct and inherited roles.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.ownedAttribute
descriptions: The Properties owned by the StructuredClassifier.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.ownedConnector
descriptions: The connectors owned by the StructuredClassifier.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.part
descriptions: The Properties specifying instances that the StructuredClassifier owns by composition. This collection is derived, selecting those owned Properties where isComposite is true.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier.role
descriptions: The roles that instances may play in this StructuredClassifier.

definitions.name: StructuredClassifier
descriptions: StructuredClassifiers may contain an internal structure of connected elements each of which plays a role in the overall Behavior modeled by the StructuredClassifier.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith() specifies a ConnectionPointReference can only be redefined by a ConnectionPointReference.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.exit_pseudostates
descriptions: The exit Pseudostates must be Pseudostates with kind exitPoint.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.entry_pseudostates
descriptions: The entry Pseudostates must be Pseudostates with kind entryPoint.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.entry
descriptions: The entryPoint Pseudostates corresponding to this connection point.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.exit
descriptions: The exitPoints kind Pseudostates corresponding to this connection point.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference.state
descriptions: The State in which the ConnectionPointReference is defined.

definitions.name: ConnectionPointReference
descriptions: A ConnectionPointReference represents a usage (as part of a submachine State) of an entry/exit point Pseudostate defined in the StateMachine referenced by the submachine State.

definitions.name: FinalState.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith() specifies a FinalState can only be redefined by a FinalState.

definitions.name: FinalState.no_exit_behavior
descriptions: A FinalState has no exit Behavior.

definitions.name: FinalState.no_outgoing_transitions
descriptions: A FinalState cannot have any outgoing Transitions.

definitions.name: FinalState.no_regions
descriptions: A FinalState cannot have Regions.

definitions.name: FinalState.cannot_reference_submachine
descriptions: A FinalState cannot reference a submachine.

definitions.name: FinalState.no_entry_behavior
descriptions: A FinalState has no entry Behavior.

definitions.name: FinalState.no_state_behavior
descriptions: A FinalState has no state (doActivity) Behavior.

definitions.name: FinalState
descriptions: A special kind of State, which, when entered, signifies that the enclosing Region has completed. If the enclosing Region is directly contained in a StateMachine and all other Regions in that StateMachine also are completed, then it means that the entire StateMachine behavior is completed.

definitions.name: ProtocolConformance.generalMachine
descriptions: Specifies the ProtocolStateMachine to which the specific ProtocolStateMachine conforms.

definitions.name: ProtocolConformance.specificMachine
descriptions: Specifies the ProtocolStateMachine which conforms to the general ProtocolStateMachine.

definitions.name: ProtocolConformance
descriptions: A ProtocolStateMachine can be redefined into a more specific ProtocolStateMachine or into behavioral StateMachine. ProtocolConformance declares that the specific ProtocolStateMachine specifies a protocol that conforms to the general ProtocolStateMachine or that the specific behavioral StateMachine abides by the protocol of the general ProtocolStateMachine.
definitions.limitation: Specific/general machine links are represented. Behavioral protocol-conformance proof is not implemented.

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine.classifier_context
descriptions: A ProtocolStateMachine must only have a Classifier context, not a BehavioralFeature context.

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine.deep_or_shallow_history
descriptions: ProtocolStateMachines cannot have deep or shallow history Pseudostates.

expressions.body:
region->forAll (r | r.subvertex->forAll (v | v.oclIsKindOf(Pseudostate) implies
((v.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind <>  PseudostateKind::deepHistory) and (v.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind <> PseudostateKind::shallowHistory))))

definitions.limitation: The source checks top-level regions only. Python applies the machine-wide prohibition in the prose to nested owned regions as well.

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine.entry_exit_do
descriptions: The states of a ProtocolStateMachine cannot have entry, exit, or do activity Behaviors.

expressions.body:
region->forAll(r | r.subvertex->forAll(v | v.oclIsKindOf(State) implies
(v.oclAsType(State).entry->isEmpty() and v.oclAsType(State).exit->isEmpty() and v.oclAsType(State).doActivity->isEmpty())))

definitions.limitation: The source checks top-level states only. Python checks states in every nested owned region according to the machine-wide prose.

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine.protocol_transitions
descriptions: All Transitions of a ProtocolStateMachine must be ProtocolTransitions.
definitions.limitation: The source checks top-level regions only. Python checks exact ProtocolTransition types in every nested owned region.

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine.conformance
descriptions: Conformance between ProtocolStateMachine

definitions.name: ProtocolStateMachine
descriptions: A ProtocolStateMachine is always defined in the context of a Classifier. It specifies which BehavioralFeatures of the Classifier can be called in which State and under which conditions, thus specifying the allowed invocation sequences on the Classifier's BehavioralFeatures. A ProtocolStateMachine specifies the possible and permitted Transitions on the instances of its context Classifier, together with the BehavioralFeatures that carry the Transitions. In this manner, an instance lifecycle can be specified for a Classifier, by defining the order in which the BehavioralFeatures can be activated and the States through which an instance progresses during its existence.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.referred
descriptions: Derivation for ProtocolTransition::/referred

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.refers_to_operation
descriptions: If a ProtocolTransition refers to an Operation (i.e., has a CallEvent trigger corresponding to an Operation), then that Operation should apply to the context Classifier of the StateMachine of the ProtocolTransition.

expressions.body:
if (referred()->notEmpty() and containingStateMachine()._'context'->notEmpty()) then 
    containingStateMachine()._'context'.oclAsType(BehavioredClassifier).allFeatures()->includesAll(referred())
else true endif

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.associated_actions
descriptions: A ProtocolTransition never has associated Behaviors.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.belongs_to_psm
descriptions: A ProtocolTransition always belongs to a ProtocolStateMachine.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.postCondition
descriptions: Specifies the post condition of the Transition which is the Condition that should be obtained once the Transition is triggered. This post condition is part of the post condition of the Operation connected to the Transition.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.preCondition
descriptions: Specifies the precondition of the Transition. It specifies the Condition that should be verified before triggering the Transition. This guard condition added to the source State will be evaluated as part of the precondition of the Operation referred by the Transition if any.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition.referred
descriptions: This association refers to the associated Operation. It is derived from the Operation of the CallEvent Trigger when applicable.

definitions.name: ProtocolTransition
descriptions: A ProtocolTransition specifies a legal Transition for an Operation. Transitions of ProtocolStateMachines have the following information: a pre-condition (guard), a Trigger, and a post-condition. Every ProtocolTransition is associated with at most one BehavioralFeature belonging to the context Classifier of the ProtocolStateMachine.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith() specifies a Pseudostate can only be redefined by a Pseudostate of the same kind.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.transitions_outgoing
descriptions: All transitions outgoing a fork vertex must target states in different regions of an orthogonal state.

expressions.body:
(kind = PseudostateKind::fork) implies

-- for any pair of outgoing transitions there exists an orthogonal state which contains the targets of these transitions 
-- such that these targets belong to different regions of that orthogonal state 

outgoing->forAll(t1:Transition, t2:Transition | let contState:State = containingStateMachine().LCAState(t1.target, t2.target) in
	((contState <> null) and (contState.region
		->exists(r1:Region, r2: Region | (r1 <> r2) and t1.target.isContainedInRegion(r1) and t2.target.isContainedInRegion(r2)))))

definitions.limitation: The source pairs a transition with itself. Python checks distinct transition pairs as the any-pair prose requires.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.choice_vertex
descriptions: In a complete statemachine, a choice Vertex must have at least one incoming and one outgoing Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.outgoing_from_initial
descriptions: The outgoing Transition from an initial vertex may have a behavior, but not a trigger or a guard.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.join_vertex
descriptions: In a complete StateMachine, a join Vertex must have at least two incoming Transitions and exactly one outgoing Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.junction_vertex
descriptions: In a complete StateMachine, a junction Vertex must have at least one incoming and one outgoing Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.history_vertices
descriptions: History Vertices can have at most one outgoing Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.initial_vertex
descriptions: An initial Vertex can have at most one outgoing Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.fork_vertex
descriptions: In a complete StateMachine, a fork Vertex must have at least two outgoing Transitions and exactly one incoming Transition.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.transitions_incoming
descriptions: All Transitions incoming a join Vertex must originate in different Regions of an orthogonal State.

expressions.body:
(kind = PseudostateKind::join) implies

-- for any pair of incoming transitions there exists an orthogonal state which contains the source vetices of these transitions 
-- such that these source vertices belong to different regions of that orthogonal state 

incoming->forAll(t1:Transition, t2:Transition | let contState:State = containingStateMachine().LCAState(t1.source, t2.source) in
	((contState <> null) and (contState.region
		->exists(r1:Region, r2: Region | (r1 <> r2) and t1.source.isContainedInRegion(r1) and t2.source.isContainedInRegion(r2)))))

definitions.limitation: The source pairs a transition with itself. Python checks distinct transition pairs as the any-pair prose requires.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.kind
descriptions: Determines the precise type of the Pseudostate and can be one of: entryPoint, exitPoint, initial, deepHistory, shallowHistory, join, fork, junction, terminate or choice.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.state
descriptions: The State that owns this Pseudostate and in which it appears.

definitions.name: Pseudostate.stateMachine
descriptions: The StateMachine in which this Pseudostate is defined. This only applies to Pseudostates of the kind entryPoint or exitPoint.

definitions.name: Pseudostate
descriptions: A Pseudostate is an abstraction that encompasses different types of transient Vertices in the StateMachine graph. A StateMachine instance never comes to rest in a Pseudostate, instead, it will exit and enter the Pseudostate within a single run-to-completion step.

definitions.name: Region.belongsToPSM
descriptions: The operation belongsToPSM () checks if the Region belongs to a ProtocolStateMachine.

expressions.body:
result = (if  stateMachine <> null 
then
  stateMachine.oclIsKindOf(ProtocolStateMachine)
else 
  state <> null  implies  state.container.belongsToPSM()
endif )

definitions.limitation: An unowned region vacuously satisfies the implication in the body. Python requires a represented containing machine; missing ownership remains invalid.

definitions.name: Region.containingStateMachine
descriptions: The operation containingStateMachine() returns the StateMachine in which this Region is defined.

expressions.body:
result = (if stateMachine = null 
then
  state.containingStateMachine()
else
  stateMachine
endif)

definitions.name: Region.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith specifies that a Region can be redefined by any Region for which the redefinition context is valid (see the isRedefinitionContextValid operation). Note that consistency requirements for the redefinition of Vertices and Transitions within a redefining Region are specified by the isConsistentWith and isRedefinitionContextValid operations for Vertex (and its subclasses) and Transition.

definitions.name: Region.isRedefinitionContextValid
descriptions: The query isRedefinitionContextValid() specifies whether the redefinition contexts of a Region are properly related to the redefinition contexts of the specified Region to allow this element to redefine the other. The containing StateMachine or State of a redefining Region must Redefine the containing StateMachine or State of the redefined Region.

expressions.body:
result = (if redefinedElement.oclIsKindOf(Region) then
  let redefinedRegion : Region = redefinedElement.oclAsType(Region) in
    if stateMachine->isEmpty() then
    -- the Region is owned by a State
      (state.redefinedState->notEmpty() and state.redefinedState.region->includes(redefinedRegion))
    else -- the region is owned by a StateMachine
      (stateMachine.extendedStateMachine->notEmpty() and
        stateMachine.extendedStateMachine->exists(sm : StateMachine |
          sm.region->includes(redefinedRegion)))
    endif
else
  false
endif)

definitions.limitation: The source references nonexistent State.redefinedState. Python uses the inherited redefinedVertex link and checks that its target is a State.

definitions.name: Region.redefinitionContext
descriptions: The redefinition context of a Region is the nearest containing StateMachine.

definitions.name: Region.deep_history_vertex
descriptions: A Region can have at most one deep history Vertex.

definitions.name: Region.shallow_history_vertex
descriptions: A Region can have at most one shallow history Vertex.

definitions.name: Region.owned
descriptions: If a Region is owned by a StateMachine, then it cannot also be owned by a State and vice versa.

expressions.body: (stateMachine <> null implies state = null) and (state <> null implies stateMachine = null)

definitions.name: Region.initial_vertex
descriptions: A Region can have at most one initial Vertex.

definitions.name: Region.extendedRegion
descriptions: The region of which this region is an extension.

definitions.name: Region.redefinitionContext
descriptions: References the Classifier in which context this element may be redefined.

definitions.name: Region.state
descriptions: The State that owns the Region. If a Region is owned by a State, then it cannot also be owned by a StateMachine.

definitions.name: Region.stateMachine
descriptions: The StateMachine that owns the Region. If a Region is owned by a StateMachine, then it cannot also be owned by a State.

definitions.name: Region.subvertex
descriptions: The set of Vertices that are owned by this Region.

definitions.name: Region.transition
descriptions: The set of Transitions owned by the Region.

definitions.name: Region
descriptions: A Region is a top-level part of a StateMachine or a composite State, that serves as a container for the Vertices and Transitions of the StateMachine. A StateMachine or composite State may contain multiple Regions representing behaviors that may occur in parallel.

definitions.name: State.containingStateMachine
descriptions: The query containingStateMachine() returns the StateMachine that contains the State either directly or transitively.

definitions.name: State.isComposite
descriptions: A composite State is a State with at least one Region.

definitions.name: State.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith specifies that a non-final State can only be redefined by a non-final State (this is overridden by FinalState to allow a FinalState to be redefined by a FinalState) and, if the redefined State is a submachine State, then the redefining State must be a submachine state whose submachine is a redefinition of the submachine of the redefined State. Note that consistency requirements for the redefinition of Regions and connectionPoint Pseudostates within a composite State and connection ConnectionPoints of a submachine State are specified by the isConsistentWith and isRedefinitionContextValid operations for Region and Vertex (and its subclasses, Pseudostate and ConnectionPointReference).

expressions.body:
result = (redefiningElement.oclIsTypeOf(State) and 
  let redefiningState : State = redefiningElement.oclAsType(State) in
    submachine <> null implies (redefiningState.submachine <> null and
      redefiningState.submachine.extendedStateMachine->includes(submachine)))

definitions.name: State.isOrthogonal
descriptions: An orthogonal State is a composite state with at least 2 regions.

definitions.name: State.isSimple
descriptions: A simple State is a State without any regions.

definitions.name: State.isSubmachineState
descriptions: Only submachine State references another StateMachine.

definitions.name: State.entry_or_exit
descriptions: Only entry or exit Pseudostates can serve as connection points.

definitions.name: State.submachine_states
descriptions: Only submachine States can have connection point references.

definitions.name: State.composite_states
descriptions: Only composite States can have entry or exit Pseudostates defined.

definitions.name: State.destinations_or_sources_of_transitions
descriptions: The connection point references used as destinations/sources of Transitions associated with a submachine State must be defined as entry/exit points in the submachine StateMachine.

expressions.body:
self.isSubmachineState implies (self.connection->forAll (cp |
  cp.entry->forAll (ps | ps.stateMachine = self.submachine) and
  cp.exit->forAll (ps | ps.stateMachine = self.submachine)))

definitions.name: State.submachine_or_regions
descriptions: A State is not allowed to have both a submachine and Regions.

definitions.name: State.connection
descriptions: The entry and exit connection points used in conjunction with this (submachine) State, i.e., as targets and sources, respectively, in the Region with the submachine State. A connection point reference references the corresponding definition of a connection point Pseudostate in the StateMachine referenced by the submachine State.

definitions.name: State.connectionPoint
descriptions: The entry and exit Pseudostates of a composite State. These can only be entry or exit Pseudostates, and they must have different names. They can only be defined for composite States.

definitions.name: State.deferrableTrigger
descriptions: A list of Triggers that are candidates to be retained by the StateMachine if they trigger no Transitions out of the State (not consumed). A deferred Trigger is retained until the StateMachine reaches a State configuration where it is no longer deferred.

definitions.name: State.doActivity
descriptions: An optional Behavior that is executed while being in the State. The execution starts when this State is entered, and ceases either by itself when done, or when the State is exited, whichever comes first.

definitions.name: State.entry
descriptions: An optional Behavior that is executed whenever this State is entered regardless of the Transition taken to reach the State. If defined, entry Behaviors are always executed to completion prior to any internal Behavior or Transitions performed within the State.

definitions.name: State.exit
descriptions: An optional Behavior that is executed whenever this State is exited regardless of which Transition was taken out of the State. If defined, exit Behaviors are always executed to completion only after all internal and transition Behaviors have completed execution.

definitions.name: State.isComposite
descriptions: A state with isComposite=true is said to be a composite State. A composite State is a State that contains at least one Region.

definitions.name: State.isOrthogonal
descriptions: A State with isOrthogonal=true is said to be an orthogonal composite State An orthogonal composite State contains two or more Regions.

definitions.name: State.isSimple
descriptions: A State with isSimple=true is said to be a simple State A simple State does not have any Regions and it does not refer to any submachine StateMachine.

definitions.name: State.isSubmachineState
descriptions: A State with isSubmachineState=true is said to be a submachine State Such a State refers to another StateMachine(submachine).

definitions.name: State.region
descriptions: The Regions owned directly by the State.

definitions.name: State.stateInvariant
descriptions: Specifies conditions that are always true when this State is the current State. In ProtocolStateMachines state invariants are additional conditions to the preconditions of the outgoing Transitions, and to the postcondition of the incoming Transitions.

definitions.name: State.submachine
descriptions: The StateMachine that is to be inserted in place of the (submachine) State.

definitions.name: State
descriptions: A State models a situation during which some (usually implicit) invariant condition holds.

definitions.name: StateMachine.LCA
descriptions: The operation LCA(s1,s2) returns the Region that is the least common ancestor of Vertices s1 and s2, based on the StateMachine containment hierarchy.

expressions.body:
result = (if ancestor(s1, s2) then 
    s2.container
else
	if ancestor(s2, s1) then
	    s1.container 
	else 
	    LCA(s1.container.state, s2.container.state)
	endif
endif)

definitions.name: StateMachine.ancestor
descriptions: The query ancestor(s1, s2) checks whether Vertex s2 is an ancestor of Vertex s1.

expressions.body:
result = (if (s2 = s1) then 
	true 
else 
	if s1.container.stateMachine->notEmpty() then 
	    true
	else 
	    if s2.container.stateMachine->notEmpty() then 
	        false
	    else
	        ancestor(s1, s2.container.state)
	     endif
	 endif
endif  )

definitions.limitation: The source top-level branch reverses the direction described in prose. Python tests whether s2 encloses s1, including equality.

definitions.name: StateMachine.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith specifies that a StateMachine can be redefined by any other StateMachine for which the redefinition context is valid (see the isRedefinitionContextValid operation). Note that consistency requirements for the redefinition of Regions and connectionPoint Pseudostates owned by a StateMachine are specified by the isConsistentWith and isRedefinitionContextValid operations for Region and Vertex (and its subclass Pseudostate).

definitions.name: StateMachine.isRedefinitionContextValid
descriptions: The query isRedefinitionContextValid specifies whether the redefinition context of a StateMachine is properly related to the redefinition contexts of a StateMachine it redefines. The requirement is that the context BehavioredClassifier of a redefining StateMachine must specialize the context Classifier of the redefined StateMachine. If the redefining StateMachine does not have a context BehavioredClassifier, then then the redefining StateMachine also must not have a context BehavioredClassifier but must, instead, specialize the redefining StateMachine.

expressions.body:
result = (redefinedElement.oclIsKindOf(StateMachine) and
  let parentContext : BehavioredClassifier =
    redefinedElement.oclAsType(StateMachine).context in
  if context = null then
    parentContext = null and self.allParents()→includes(redefinedElement)
  else
    parentContext <> null and context.allParents()->includes(parentContext)
  endif)

definitions.name: StateMachine.LCAState
descriptions: This utility funciton is like the LCA, except that it returns the nearest composite State that contains both input Vertices.

expressions.body:
result = (if v2.oclIsTypeOf(State) and ancestor(v1, v2) then
	v2.oclAsType(State)
else if v1.oclIsTypeOf(State) and ancestor(v2, v1) then
	v1.oclAsType(State)
else if (v1.container.state->isEmpty() or v2.container.state->isEmpty()) then 
	null.oclAsType(State)
else LCAState(v1.container.state, v2.container.state)
endif endif endif)

definitions.limitation: The body explicitly returns null when no common enclosing State exists, despite a mandatory result signature.

definitions.name: StateMachine.connection_points
descriptions: The connection points of a StateMachine are Pseudostates of kind entry point or exit point.

definitions.name: StateMachine.classifier_context
descriptions: The Classifier context of a StateMachine cannot be an Interface.

definitions.name: StateMachine.method
descriptions: A StateMachine as the method for a BehavioralFeature cannot have entry/exit connection points.

definitions.name: StateMachine.context_classifier
descriptions: The context Classifier of the method StateMachine of a BehavioralFeature must be the Classifier that owns the BehavioralFeature.

expressions.body: specification <> null implies ( _'context' <> null and specification.featuringClassifier->exists(c | c = _'context'))

definitions.name: StateMachine.connectionPoint
descriptions: The connection points defined for this StateMachine. They represent the interface of the StateMachine when used as part of submachine State

definitions.name: StateMachine.extendedStateMachine
descriptions: The StateMachines of which this is an extension.

definitions.name: StateMachine.region
descriptions: The Regions owned directly by the StateMachine.

definitions.name: StateMachine.submachineState
descriptions: References the submachine(s) in case of a submachine State. Multiple machines are referenced in case of a concurrent State.

definitions.name: StateMachine
descriptions: StateMachines can be used to express event-driven behaviors of parts of a system. Behavior is modeled as a traversal of a graph of Vertices interconnected by one or more joined Transition arcs that are triggered by the dispatching of successive Event occurrences. During this traversal, the StateMachine may execute a sequence of Behaviors associated with various elements of the StateMachine.

definitions.name: Transition.containingStateMachine
descriptions: The query containingStateMachine() returns the StateMachine that contains the Transition either directly or transitively.

definitions.name: Transition.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isConsistentWith specifies that a redefining Transition is consistent with a redefined Transition provided that the source Vertex of the redefining Transition redefines the source Vertex of the redefined Transition.

definitions.name: Transition.redefinitionContext
descriptions: The redefinition context of a Transition is the nearest containing StateMachine.

definitions.name: Transition.state_is_external
descriptions: A Transition with kind external can source any Vertex except entry points.

expressions.body:
(kind = TransitionKind::external) implies
	not (source.oclIsKindOf(Pseudostate) and source.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::entryPoint)

definitions.name: Transition.join_segment_guards
descriptions: A join segment must not have Guards or Triggers.

expressions.body: (target.oclIsKindOf(Pseudostate) and target.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::join) implies (guard = null and trigger->isEmpty())

definitions.name: Transition.state_is_internal
descriptions: A Transition with kind internal must have a State as its source, and its source and target must be equal.

definitions.name: Transition.outgoing_pseudostates
descriptions: Transitions outgoing Pseudostates may not have a Trigger.

definitions.name: Transition.join_segment_state
descriptions: A join segment must always originate from a State.

definitions.name: Transition.fork_segment_state
descriptions: A fork segment must always target a State.

definitions.name: Transition.state_is_local
descriptions: A Transition with kind local must have a composite State or an entry point as its source.

expressions.body:
(kind = TransitionKind::local) implies
		((source.oclIsKindOf (State) and source.oclAsType(State).isComposite) or
		(source.oclIsKindOf (Pseudostate) and source.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::entryPoint))

definitions.name: Transition.initial_transition
descriptions: An initial Transition at the topmost level Region of a StateMachine that has no Trigger.

definitions.name: Transition.fork_segment_guards
descriptions: A fork segment must not have Guards or Triggers.

expressions.body: (source.oclIsKindOf(Pseudostate) and source.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::fork) implies (guard = null and trigger->isEmpty())

definitions.name: Transition.transition_vertices
descriptions: The source and target Vertices of a Transition must be contained in the same StateMachine as the Transition.

expressions.body:
let stateMachine = self.containingStateMachine() in 
source.containingStateMachine() = stateMachine and 
target.containingStateMachine() = stateMachine

definitions.name: Transition.container
descriptions: Designates the Region that owns this Transition.

definitions.name: Transition.effect
descriptions: Specifies an optional behavior to be performed when the Transition fires.

definitions.name: Transition.guard
descriptions: A guard is a Constraint that provides a fine-grained control over the firing of the Transition. The guard is evaluated when an Event occurrence is dispatched by the StateMachine. If the guard is true at that time, the Transition may be enabled, otherwise, it is disabled. Guards should be pure expressions without side effects. Guard expressions with side effects are ill formed.

definitions.name: Transition.kind
descriptions: Indicates the precise type of the Transition.

definitions.name: Transition.redefinedTransition
descriptions: The Transition that is redefined by this Transition.

definitions.name: Transition.redefinitionContext
descriptions: References the Classifier in which context this element may be redefined.

definitions.name: Transition.source
descriptions: Designates the originating Vertex (State or Pseudostate) of the Transition.

definitions.name: Transition.target
descriptions: Designates the target Vertex that is reached when the Transition is taken.

definitions.name: Transition.trigger
descriptions: Specifies the Triggers that may fire the transition.

definitions.name: Transition
descriptions: A Transition represents an arc between exactly one source Vertex and exactly one Target vertex (the source and targets may be the same Vertex). It may form part of a compound transition, which takes the StateMachine from one steady State configuration to another, representing the full response of the StateMachine to an occurrence of an Event that triggered it.

definitions.name: Vertex.containingStateMachine
descriptions: The operation containingStateMachine() returns the StateMachine in which this Vertex is defined.

expressions.body:
result = (if container <> null
then
-- the container is a region
   container.containingStateMachine()
else 
   if (self.oclIsKindOf(Pseudostate)) and ((self.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::entryPoint) or (self.oclAsType(Pseudostate).kind = PseudostateKind::exitPoint)) then
      self.oclAsType(Pseudostate).stateMachine
   else 
      if (self.oclIsKindOf(ConnectionPointReference)) then
          self.oclAsType(ConnectionPointReference).state.containingStateMachine() -- no other valid cases possible
      else 
          null
      endif
   endif
endif

)

definitions.limitation: The source omits entry/exit points owned by composite States. Python follows the represented State owner to its containing machine.

definitions.name: Vertex.incoming
descriptions: Derivation for Vertex::/incoming.

definitions.name: Vertex.outgoing
descriptions: Derivation for Vertex::/outgoing

definitions.name: Vertex.isContainedInState
descriptions: This utility operation returns true if the Vertex is contained in the State s (input argument).

expressions.body:
result = (if not s.isComposite() or container->isEmpty() then
	false
else
	if container.state = s then 
		true
	else
		container.state.isContainedInState(s)
	endif
endif)

definitions.name: Vertex.isContainedInRegion
descriptions: This utility query returns true if the Vertex is contained in the Region r (input argument).

expressions.body:
result = (if (container = r) then
	true
else
	if (r.state->isEmpty()) then
		false
	else
		container.state.isContainedInRegion(r)
	endif
endif)

definitions.limitation: The source recursion tests the queried region instead of progressing through the vertex containers. Python walks the actual enclosing regions.

definitions.name: Vertex.redefinitionContext
descriptions: The redefinition context of a Vertex is the nearest containing StateMachine.

definitions.name: Vertex.isConsistentWith
descriptions: The query isRedefinitionContextValid specifies that the redefinition context of a redefining Vertex is properly related to the redefinition context of the redefined Vertex if the owner of the redefining Vertex is a redefinition of the owner of the redefined Vertex. Note that the owner of a Vertex may be a Region, a StateMachine (for a connectionPoint Pseudostate), or a State (for a connectionPoint Pseudostate or a connection ConnectionPointReference), all of which are RedefinableElements.
definitions.limitation: The operation has duplicate State-prefixed XMI identifiers and refers to an undeclared redefinedElement. Python uses the redefiningElement argument and the represented owner redefinition relation.

definitions.name: Vertex.container
descriptions: The Region that contains this Vertex.

definitions.name: Vertex.incoming
descriptions: Specifies the Transitions entering this Vertex.

definitions.name: Vertex.outgoing
descriptions: Specifies the Transitions departing from this Vertex.

definitions.name: Vertex.redefinitionContext
descriptions: References the Classifier in which context this element may be redefined.

definitions.name: Vertex.redefinedVertex
descriptions: The Vertex of which this Vertex is a redefinition.

definitions.name: Vertex
descriptions: A Vertex is an abstraction of a node in a StateMachine graph. It can be the source or destination of any number of Transitions.

definitions.name: BehavioredClassifier.class_behavior
descriptions: If a behavior is classifier behavior, it does not have a specification.

definitions.name: BehavioredClassifier.classifierBehavior
descriptions: A Behavior that specifies the behavior of the BehavioredClassifier itself.

definitions.name: BehavioredClassifier.interfaceRealization
descriptions: The set of InterfaceRealizations owned by the BehavioredClassifier. Interface realizations reference the Interfaces of which the BehavioredClassifier is an implementation.

definitions.name: BehavioredClassifier.ownedBehavior
descriptions: Behaviors owned by a BehavioredClassifier.

definitions.name: BehavioredClassifier
descriptions: A BehavioredClassifier may have InterfaceRealizations, and owns a set of Behaviors one of which may specify the behavior of the BehavioredClassifier itself.

definitions.name: DataType.ownedAttribute
descriptions: The attributes owned by the DataType.

definitions.name: DataType.ownedOperation
descriptions: The Operations owned by the DataType.

definitions.name: DataType
descriptions: A DataType is a type whose instances are identified only by their value.

definitions.name: Enumeration.ownedLiteral
descriptions: The ordered set of literals owned by this Enumeration.

definitions.name: Enumeration
descriptions: An Enumeration is a DataType whose values are enumerated in the model as EnumerationLiterals.

definitions.name: EnumerationLiteral.classifier
descriptions: Derivation of Enumeration::/classifier

definitions.name: EnumerationLiteral.classifier
descriptions: The classifier of this EnumerationLiteral derived to be equal to its Enumeration.

definitions.name: EnumerationLiteral.enumeration
descriptions: The Enumeration that this EnumerationLiteral is a member of.

definitions.name: EnumerationLiteral
descriptions: An EnumerationLiteral is a user-defined data value for an Enumeration.

definitions.name: Interface.visibility
descriptions: The visibility of all Features owned by an Interface must be public.

definitions.name: Interface.nestedClassifier
descriptions: References all the Classifiers that are defined (nested) within the Interface.

definitions.name: Interface.ownedAttribute
descriptions: The attributes (i.e., the Properties) owned by the Interface.

definitions.name: Interface.ownedOperation
descriptions: The Operations owned by the Interface.

definitions.name: Interface.ownedReception
descriptions: Receptions that objects providing this Interface are willing to accept.

definitions.name: Interface.protocol
descriptions: References a ProtocolStateMachine specifying the legal sequences of the invocation of the BehavioralFeatures described in the Interface.

definitions.name: Interface.redefinedInterface
descriptions: References all the Interfaces redefined by this Interface.

definitions.name: Interface
descriptions: Interfaces declare coherent services that are implemented by BehavioredClassifiers that implement the Interfaces via InterfaceRealizations.

definitions.name: InterfaceRealization.contract
descriptions: References the Interface specifying the conformance contract.

definitions.name: InterfaceRealization.implementingClassifier
descriptions: References the BehavioredClassifier that owns this InterfaceRealization, i.e., the BehavioredClassifier that realizes the Interface to which it refers.

definitions.name: InterfaceRealization
descriptions: An InterfaceRealization is a specialized realization relationship between a BehavioredClassifier and an Interface. This relationship signifies that the realizing BehavioredClassifier conforms to the contract specified by the Interface.

definitions.name: PrimitiveType
descriptions: A PrimitiveType defines a predefined DataType, without any substructure. A PrimitiveType may have an algebra and operations defined outside of UML, for example, mathematically.

definitions.name: Reception.same_name_as_signal
descriptions: A Reception has the same name as its signal

definitions.name: Reception.same_structure_as_signal
descriptions: A Reception's parameters match the ownedAttributes of its signal by name, type, and multiplicity

expressions.body:
signal.ownedAttribute->size() = ownedParameter->size() and
Sequence{1..signal.ownedAttribute->size()}->forAll( i | 
    ownedParameter->at(i).direction = ParameterDirectionKind::_'in' and 
    ownedParameter->at(i).name = signal.ownedAttribute->at(i).name and
    ownedParameter->at(i).type = signal.ownedAttribute->at(i).type and
    ownedParameter->at(i).lowerBound() = signal.ownedAttribute->at(i).lowerBound() and
    ownedParameter->at(i).upperBound() = signal.ownedAttribute->at(i).upperBound()
)

definitions.name: Reception.signal
descriptions: The Signal that this Reception handles.

definitions.name: Reception
descriptions: A Reception is a declaration stating that a Classifier is prepared to react to the receipt of a Signal.

definitions.name: Signal.ownedAttribute
descriptions: The attributes owned by the Signal.

definitions.name: Signal
descriptions: A Signal is a specification of a kind of communication between objects in which a reaction is asynchronously triggered in the receiver without a reply.

definitions.name: Extension.isRequired
descriptions: The query isRequired() is true if the owned end has a multiplicity with the lower bound of 1.

definitions.name: Extension.metaclass
descriptions: The query metaclass() returns the metaclass that is being extended (as opposed to the extending stereotype).

definitions.name: Extension.metaclassEnd
descriptions: The query metaclassEnd() returns the Property that is typed by a metaclass (as opposed to a stereotype).

definitions.name: Extension.non_owned_end
descriptions: The non-owned end of an Extension is typed by a Class.

definitions.name: Extension.is_binary
descriptions: An Extension is binary, i.e., it has only two memberEnds.

definitions.name: Extension.isRequired
descriptions: Indicates whether an instance of the extending stereotype must be created when an instance of the extended class is created. The attribute value is derived from the value of the lower property of the ExtensionEnd referenced by Extension::ownedEnd; a lower value of 1 means that isRequired is true, but otherwise it is false. Since the default value of ExtensionEnd::lower is 0, the default value of isRequired is false.

definitions.name: Extension.metaclass
descriptions: References the Class that is extended through an Extension. The property is derived from the type of the memberEnd that is not the ownedEnd.

definitions.name: Extension.ownedEnd
descriptions: References the end of the extension that is typed by a Stereotype.

definitions.name: Extension
descriptions: An extension is used to indicate that the properties of a metaclass are extended through a stereotype, and gives the ability to flexibly add (and later remove) stereotypes to classes.

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd.lowerBound
descriptions: The query lowerBound() returns the lower bound of the multiplicity as an Integer. This is a redefinition of the default lower bound, which normally, for MultiplicityElements, evaluates to 1 if empty.

expressions.body: result = (if lowerValue=null then 0 else lowerValue.integerValue() endif)

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd.multiplicity
descriptions: The multiplicity of ExtensionEnd is 0..1 or 1.

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd.aggregation
descriptions: The aggregation of an ExtensionEnd is composite.

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd.lower
descriptions: This redefinition changes the default multiplicity of association ends, since model elements are usually extended by 0 or 1 instance of the extension stereotype.

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd.type
descriptions: References the type of the ExtensionEnd. Note that this association restricts the possible types of an ExtensionEnd to only be Stereotypes.

definitions.name: ExtensionEnd
descriptions:
An extension end is used to tie an extension to a stereotype when extending a metaclass.
The default multiplicity of an extension end is 0..1.

definitions.name: Image.content
descriptions: This contains the serialization of the image according to the format. The value could represent a bitmap, image such as a GIF file, or drawing 'instructions' using a standard such as Scalable Vector Graphic (SVG) (which is XML based).

definitions.name: Image.format
descriptions: This indicates the format of the content, which is how the string content should be interpreted. The following values are reserved: SVG, GIF, PNG, JPG, WMF, EMF, BMP. In addition the prefix 'MIME: ' is also reserved. This option can be used as an alternative to express the reserved values above, for example "SVG" could instead be expressed as "MIME: image/svg+xml".

definitions.name: Image.location
descriptions: This contains a location that can be used by a tool to locate the image as an alternative to embedding it in the stereotype.

definitions.name: Image
descriptions: Physical definition of a graphical image.

definitions.name: Model.viewpoint
descriptions: The name of the viewpoint that is expressed by a model (this name may refer to a profile definition).

definitions.name: Model
descriptions: A model captures a view of a physical system. It is an abstraction of the physical system, with a certain purpose. This purpose determines what is to be included in the model and what is irrelevant. Thus the model completely describes those aspects of the physical system that are relevant to the purpose of the model, at the appropriate level of detail.

definitions.name: Package.allApplicableStereotypes
descriptions: The query allApplicableStereotypes() returns all the directly or indirectly owned stereotypes, including stereotypes contained in sub-profiles.

definitions.name: Package.containingProfile
descriptions: The query containingProfile() returns the closest profile directly or indirectly containing this package (or this package itself, if it is a profile).

expressions.body:
result = (if self.oclIsKindOf(Profile) then 
	self.oclAsType(Profile)
else
	self.namespace.oclAsType(Package).containingProfile()
endif)

definitions.limitation: The recursive XMI body has no root/null guard. Python returns null at an unowned non-Profile Package, matching the optional result signature.

definitions.name: Package.makesVisible
descriptions: The query makesVisible() defines whether a Package makes an element visible outside itself. Elements with no visibility and elements with public visibility are made visible.
definitions.limitation: The source compares importedElement to a VisibilityKind and uses notEmpty on Booleans. Python follows the prose and explicit public-import visibility; private imports are not reexported.

definitions.name: Package.mustBeOwned
descriptions: The query mustBeOwned() indicates whether elements of this type must have an owner.

definitions.name: Package.nestedPackage
descriptions: Derivation for Package::/nestedPackage

definitions.name: Package.ownedStereotype
descriptions: Derivation for Package::/ownedStereotype

definitions.name: Package.ownedType
descriptions: Derivation for Package::/ownedType

definitions.name: Package.visibleMembers
descriptions: The query visibleMembers() defines which members of a Package can be accessed outside it.

definitions.name: Package.elements_public_or_private
descriptions: If an element that is owned by a package has visibility, it is public or private.

expressions.body: packagedElement->forAll(e | e.visibility<> null implies e.visibility = VisibilityKind::public or e.visibility = VisibilityKind::private)

definitions.name: Package.URI
descriptions: Provides an identifier for the package that can be used for many purposes. A URI is the universally unique identification of the package following the IETF URI specification, RFC 2396 http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2396.txt and it must comply with those syntax rules.

definitions.name: Package.nestedPackage
descriptions: References the packaged elements that are Packages.

definitions.name: Package.nestingPackage
descriptions: References the Package that owns this Package.

definitions.name: Package.ownedStereotype
descriptions: References the Stereotypes that are owned by the Package.

definitions.name: Package.ownedType
descriptions: References the packaged elements that are Types.

definitions.name: Package.packageMerge
descriptions: References the PackageMerges that are owned by this Package.

definitions.name: Package.packagedElement
descriptions: Specifies the packageable elements that are owned by this Package.

definitions.name: Package.profileApplication
descriptions: References the ProfileApplications that indicate which profiles have been applied to the Package.

definitions.name: Package
descriptions:
A package can have one or more profile applications to indicate which profiles have been applied. Because a profile is a package, it is possible to apply a profile not only to packages, but also to profiles.
Package specializes TemplateableElement and PackageableElement specializes ParameterableElement to specify that a package can be used as a template and a PackageableElement as a template parameter.
A package is used to group elements, and provides a namespace for the grouped elements.

definitions.name: PackageMerge.mergedPackage
descriptions: References the Package that is to be merged with the receiving package of the PackageMerge.

definitions.name: PackageMerge.receivingPackage
descriptions: References the Package that is being extended with the contents of the merged package of the PackageMerge.

definitions.name: PackageMerge
descriptions: A package merge defines how the contents of one package are extended by the contents of another package.
definitions.limitation: The model represents receiving/merged Package links. The normative reconciliation/merge algorithm is not implemented.

definitions.name: Profile.metaclass_reference_not_specialized
descriptions: An element imported as a metaclassReference is not specialized or generalized in a Profile.

expressions.body:
metaclassReference.importedElement->
	select(c | c.oclIsKindOf(Classifier) and
		(c.oclAsType(Classifier).allParents()->collect(namespace)->includes(self)))->isEmpty()
and 
packagedElement->
    select(oclIsKindOf(Classifier))->collect(oclAsType(Classifier).allParents())->
       intersection(metaclassReference.importedElement->select(oclIsKindOf(Classifier))->collect(oclAsType(Classifier)))->isEmpty()

definitions.name: Profile.references_same_metamodel
descriptions: All elements imported either as metaclassReferences or through metamodelReferences are members of the same base reference metamodel.

definitions.name: Profile.metaclassReference
descriptions: References a metaclass that may be extended.

definitions.name: Profile.metamodelReference
descriptions: References a package containing (directly or indirectly) metaclasses that may be extended.

definitions.name: Profile
descriptions: A profile defines limited extensions to a reference metamodel with the purpose of adapting the metamodel to a specific platform or domain.

definitions.name: ProfileApplication.appliedProfile
descriptions: References the Profiles that are applied to a Package through this ProfileApplication.

definitions.name: ProfileApplication.applyingPackage
descriptions: The package that owns the profile application.

definitions.name: ProfileApplication.isStrict
descriptions: Specifies that the Profile filtering rules for the metaclasses of the referenced metamodel shall be strictly applied.
definitions.limitation: Strict availability views and checked creation support UML metaclass references, imported profiles, extended subtypes and conflicting filters. Direct constructors remain available for general model editing. Non-UML metaclasses need an adapter; UI presentation and CMOF interoperability remain open.

definitions.name: ProfileApplication
descriptions: A profile application is used to show which profiles have been applied to a package.

definitions.name: Stereotype.containingProfile
descriptions: The query containingProfile returns the closest profile directly or indirectly containing this stereotype.

definitions.name: Stereotype.profile
descriptions: A stereotype must be contained, directly or indirectly, in a profile.

definitions.name: Stereotype.binaryAssociationsOnly
descriptions: Stereotypes may only participate in binary associations.

definitions.name: Stereotype.generalize
descriptions: A Stereotype may only generalize or specialize another Stereotype.

definitions.name: Stereotype.name_not_clash
descriptions: Stereotype names should not clash with keyword names for the extended model element.

definitions.name: Stereotype.associationEndOwnership
descriptions: Where a stereotype’s property is an association end for an association other than a kind of extension, and the other end is not a stereotype, the other end must be owned by the association itself.

expressions.body:
ownedAttribute
->select(association->notEmpty() and not association.oclIsKindOf(Extension) and not type.oclIsKindOf(Stereotype))
->forAll(opposite.owner = association)

definitions.name: Stereotype.base_property_upper_bound
descriptions: The upper bound of base-properties is exactly 1.

definitions.name: Stereotype.base_property_multiplicity_single_extension
descriptions: If a Stereotype extends only one metaclass, the multiplicity of the corresponding base-property shall be 1..1.

definitions.name: Stereotype.base_property_multiplicity_multiple_extension
descriptions: If a Stereotype extends more than one metaclass, the multiplicity of the corresponding base-properties shall be [0..1]. At any point in time, only one of these base-properties can contain a metaclass instance during runtime.

definitions.name: Stereotype.icon
descriptions: Stereotype can change the graphical appearance of the extended model element by using attached icons. When this association is not null, it references the location of the icon content to be displayed within diagrams presenting the extended model elements.

definitions.name: Stereotype.profile
descriptions: The profile that directly or indirectly contains this stereotype.

definitions.name: Stereotype
descriptions: A stereotype defines how an existing metaclass may be extended, and enables the use of platform or domain specific terminology or notation in place of, or in addition to, the ones used for the extended metaclass.
definitions.limitation: Runtime typed tags support effective inherited/redefined properties, literal defaults, bounds, readonly values, enumerations, profile Class/DataType objects, binary navigable inverses, composition and deletion. User constraints use trusted Python callbacks or Boolean literals, never arbitrary OCL execution. Custom primitive/derived/default evaluators, association-owned runtime navigation, full CMOF serialization and exhaustive profile semantics remain open.

definitions.name: ActionExecutionSpecification.action_referenced
descriptions: The Action referenced by the ActionExecutionSpecification must be owned by the Interaction owning that ActionExecutionSpecification.

(enclosingInteraction->notEmpty() or enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->notEmpty()) and
let parentInteraction : Set(Interaction) = enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(Interaction)->asSet()->union(
enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->closure(enclosingOperand.combinedFragment)->
collect(enclosingInteraction).oclAsType(Interaction)->asSet()) in
(parentInteraction->size() = 1) and self.action.interaction->asSet() = parentInteraction

expressions.body:
(interactionOperator =  InteractionOperatorKind::opt or interactionOperator = InteractionOperatorKind::loop or

definitions.name: CombinedFragment
descriptions: A CombinedFragment defines an expression of InteractionFragments. A CombinedFragment is defined by an interaction operator and corresponding InteractionOperands. Through the use of CombinedFragments the user will be able to describe a number of traces in a compact and concise manner.

definitions.name: ConsiderIgnoreFragment.consider_or_ignore
descriptions: The interaction operator of a ConsiderIgnoreFragment must be either 'consider' or 'ignore'.

definitions.name: Continuation.first_or_last_interaction_fragment
descriptions: Continuations always occur as the very first InteractionFragment or the very last InteractionFragment of the enclosing InteractionOperand.

expressions.body:
enclosingOperand->notEmpty() and 
 let peerFragments : OrderedSet(InteractionFragment) =  enclosingOperand.fragment in 
   ( peerFragments->notEmpty() and 
   ((peerFragments->first() = self) or  (peerFragments->last() = self)))

definitions.name: Continuation.same_name
descriptions: Across all Interaction instances having the same context value, every Lifeline instance covered by a Continuation (self) must be common with one covered Lifeline instance of all other Continuation instances with the same name as self, and every Lifeline instance covered by a Continuation instance with the same name as self must be common with one covered Lifeline instance of self. Lifeline instances are common if they have the same selector and represents associationEnd values.

expressions.body:
enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->notEmpty() and
let parentInteraction : Set(Interaction) = 
enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->closure(enclosingOperand.combinedFragment)->
collect(enclosingInteraction).oclAsType(Interaction)->asSet()
in 
(parentInteraction->size() = 1) 
and let peerInteractions : Set(Interaction) =
 (parentInteraction->union(parentInteraction->collect(_'context')->collect(behavior)->
 select(oclIsKindOf(Interaction)).oclAsType(Interaction)->asSet())->asSet()) in
 (peerInteractions->notEmpty()) and 
  let combinedFragments1 : Set(CombinedFragment) = peerInteractions.fragment->
 select(oclIsKindOf(CombinedFragment)).oclAsType(CombinedFragment)->asSet() in
   combinedFragments1->notEmpty() and  combinedFragments1->closure(operand.fragment->
   select(oclIsKindOf(CombinedFragment)).oclAsType(CombinedFragment))->asSet().operand.fragment->
   select(oclIsKindOf(Continuation)).oclAsType(Continuation)->asSet()->
   forAll(c : Continuation |  (c.name = self.name) implies 
  (c.covered->asSet()->forAll(cl : Lifeline | --  cl must be common to one lifeline covered by self
  self.covered->asSet()->
  select(represents = cl.represents and selector = cl.selector)->asSet()->size()=1))
   and
 (self.covered->asSet()->forAll(cl : Lifeline | --  cl must be common to one lifeline covered by c
 c.covered->asSet()->
  select(represents = cl.represents and selector = cl.selector)->asSet()->size()=1))
  )

definitions.limitation: Peer traversal uses context-owned Interactions and role identity with literal selector kind/value. A complete census of every Interaction sharing context and arbitrary domain selector equivalence remains open.

definitions.name: Continuation.global
descriptions: Continuations are always global in the enclosing InteractionFragment e.g., it always covers all Lifelines covered by the enclosing InteractionOperator.

expressions.body:
enclosingOperand->notEmpty() and
  let operandLifelines : Set(Lifeline) =  enclosingOperand.covered in 
    (operandLifelines->notEmpty() and 
    operandLifelines->forAll(ol :Lifeline |self.covered->includes(ol)))

definitions.name: Continuation.setting
descriptions: True: when the Continuation is at the end of the enclosing InteractionFragment and False when it is in the beginning.

definitions.name: Continuation
descriptions: A Continuation is a syntactic way to define continuations of different branches of an alternative CombinedFragment. Continuations are intuitively similar to labels representing intermediate points in a flow of control.

definitions.name: DestructionOccurrenceSpecification.no_occurrence_specifications_below

definitions.name: DestructionOccurrenceSpecification
