definitions.name: ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification.execution
descriptions: References the execution specification describing the execution that is started or finished at this execution event.

definitions.name: ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification
descriptions: An ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification represents moments in time at which Actions or Behaviors start or finish.

definitions.name: ExecutionSpecification.same_lifeline
descriptions: The startEvent and the finishEvent must be on the same Lifeline.

definitions.name: ExecutionSpecification.finish
descriptions: References the OccurrenceSpecification that designates the finish of the Action or Behavior.

definitions.name: ExecutionSpecification.start
descriptions: References the OccurrenceSpecification that designates the start of the Action or Behavior.

definitions.name: ExecutionSpecification
descriptions: An ExecutionSpecification is a specification of the execution of a unit of Behavior or Action within the Lifeline. The duration of an ExecutionSpecification is represented by two OccurrenceSpecifications, the start OccurrenceSpecification and the finish OccurrenceSpecification.

definitions.name: Gate.isOutsideCF
descriptions: This query returns true if this Gate is attached to the boundary of a CombinedFragment, and its other end (if present)  is outside of the same CombinedFragment.

expressions.body:
result = (self.oppositeEnd()-> notEmpty() and combinedFragment->notEmpty() implies
let oppEnd : MessageEnd = self.oppositeEnd()->asOrderedSet()->first() in
if oppEnd.oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification) 
then let oppMOS : MessageOccurrenceSpecification = oppEnd.oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
in  self.combinedFragment.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(self.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()) =
     oppMOS.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(oppMOS.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet())
else let oppGate : Gate = oppEnd.oclAsType(Gate) 
in self.combinedFragment.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(self.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()) =
     oppGate.combinedFragment.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(oppGate.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet())
endif)

definitions.limitation: The source implication vacuously returns true without an opposite end or CombinedFragment. Python requires both and represented surrounding ownership, according to the query description.

definitions.name: Gate.isInsideCF
descriptions: This query returns true if this Gate is attached to the boundary of a CombinedFragment, and its other end (if present) is inside of an InteractionOperator of the same CombinedFragment.

expressions.body:
result = (self.oppositeEnd()-> notEmpty() and combinedFragment->notEmpty() implies
let oppEnd : MessageEnd = self.oppositeEnd()->asOrderedSet()->first() in
if oppEnd.oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
then let oppMOS : MessageOccurrenceSpecification
= oppEnd.oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
in combinedFragment = oppMOS.enclosingOperand.combinedFragment
else let oppGate : Gate = oppEnd.oclAsType(Gate)
in combinedFragment = oppGate.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand.combinedFragment
endif)

definitions.limitation: The source implication vacuously returns true without an opposite end or CombinedFragment. Python follows the query description and returns false when these prerequisites are absent.

definitions.name: Gate.isActual
descriptions: This query returns true value if this Gate is an actualGate of an InteractionUse.

definitions.name: Gate.isFormal
descriptions: This query returns true if this Gate is a formalGate of an Interaction.
interaction->notEmpty()

definitions.name: Gate.getName
descriptions: This query returns the name of the gate, either the explicit name (.name) or the constructed name ('out_" or 'in_' concatenated in front of .message.name) if the explicit name is not present.

definitions.name: Gate.matches
descriptions: This query returns true if the name of this Gate matches the name of the in parameter Gate, and the messages for the two Gates correspond. The Message for one Gate (say A) corresponds to the Message for another Gate (say B) if (A and B have the same name value) and (if A is a sendEvent then B is a receiveEvent) and (if A is a receiveEvent then B is a sendEvent) and (A and B have the same messageSort value) and (A and B have the same signature value).

expressions.body:
result = (self.getName() = gateToMatch.getName() and 
self.message.messageSort = gateToMatch.message.messageSort and
self.message.name = gateToMatch.message.name and
self.message.sendEvent->includes(self) implies gateToMatch.message.receiveEvent->includes(gateToMatch)  and
self.message.receiveEvent->includes(self) implies gateToMatch.message.sendEvent->includes(gateToMatch) and
self.message.signature = gateToMatch.message.signature)

definitions.limitation: Python parenthesizes the directional implications so that all name, message-sort and signature checks apply together, according to the query description.

definitions.name: Gate.isDistinguishableFrom
descriptions:
The query isDistinguishableFrom() specifies that two Gates may coexist in the same Namespace, without an explicit name property. The association end formalGate subsets ownedElement, and since the Gate name attribute
is optional, it is allowed to have two formal gates without an explicit name, but having derived names which are distinct.

definitions.name: Gate.getOperand
descriptions: If the Gate is an inside Combined Fragment Gate, this operation returns the InteractionOperand that the opposite end of this Gate is included within.

expressions.body:
result = (if isInsideCF() then
  let oppEnd : MessageEnd = self.oppositeEnd()->asOrderedSet()->first() in
    if oppEnd.oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
    then let oppMOS : MessageOccurrenceSpecification = oppEnd.oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
        in oppMOS.enclosingOperand->asOrderedSet()->first()
    else let oppGate : Gate = oppEnd.oclAsType(Gate)
        in oppGate.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand->asOrderedSet()->first()
    endif
  else null
endif)

definitions.limitation: The body explicitly returns null for gates that are not inside a CombinedFragment, despite a mandatory result signature.

definitions.name: Gate.actual_gate_matched
descriptions: If this Gate is an actualGate, it must have exactly one matching formalGate within the referred Interaction.

definitions.name: Gate.inside_cf_matched
descriptions: If this Gate is inside a CombinedFragment, it must have exactly one matching Gate which is outside of that CombinedFragment.

definitions.name: Gate.outside_cf_matched
descriptions: If this Gate is outside an 'alt' CombinedFragment,  for every InteractionOperator inside that CombinedFragment there must be exactly one matching Gate inside the CombindedFragment with its opposing end enclosed by that InteractionOperator. If this Gate is outside CombinedFragment with operator other than 'alt',   there must be exactly one matching Gate inside that CombinedFragment.

expressions.body:
isOutsideCF() implies
 if self.combinedFragment.interactionOperator->asOrderedSet()->first() = InteractionOperatorKind::alt
 then self.combinedFragment.operand->forAll(op : InteractionOperand |
 self.combinedFragment.cfragmentGate->select(isInsideCF() and 
 oppositeEnd().enclosingFragment()->includes(self.combinedFragment) and matches(self))->size()=1)
 else  self.combinedFragment.cfragmentGate->select(isInsideCF() and matches(self))->size()=1
 endif

definitions.limitation: The alt branch does not use its operand variable and tests an enclosing-fragment relation that misses the operand. Python requires one matching inside gate per operand as the prose specifies.

definitions.name: Gate.formal_gate_distinguishable
descriptions: isFormal() implies that no other formalGate of the parent Interaction returns the same getName() as returned for self

definitions.name: Gate.actual_gate_distinguishable
descriptions: isActual() implies that no other actualGate of the parent InteractionUse returns the same getName() as returned for self

definitions.name: Gate.outside_cf_gate_distinguishable
descriptions: isOutsideCF() implies that no other outside cfragmentGate of the parent CombinedFragment returns the same getName() as returned for self
definitions.limitation: The source counts inside gates as well. Python compares outside gates only, as the prose requires; inside/outside pairs may share the matching name.

definitions.name: Gate.inside_cf_gate_distinguishable
descriptions: isInsideCF() implies that no other inside cfragmentGate attached to a message with its other end in the same InteractionOperator as self, returns the same getName() as returned for self

expressions.body:
isInsideCF() implies
let selfOperand : InteractionOperand = self.getOperand() in
  combinedFragment.cfragmentGate->select(isInsideCF() and getName() = self.getName())->select(getOperand() = selfOperand)->size()=1

definitions.name: Gate
descriptions: A Gate is a MessageEnd which serves as a connection point for relating a Message which has a MessageEnd (sendEvent / receiveEvent) outside an InteractionFragment with another Message which has a MessageEnd (receiveEvent / sendEvent)  inside that InteractionFragment.

definitions.name: GeneralOrdering.irreflexive_transitive_closure
descriptions: An occurrence specification must not be ordered relative to itself through a series of general orderings. (In other words, the transitive closure of the general orderings is irreflexive.)

definitions.name: GeneralOrdering.after
descriptions: The OccurrenceSpecification referenced comes after the OccurrenceSpecification referenced by before.

definitions.name: GeneralOrdering.before
descriptions: The OccurrenceSpecification referenced comes before the OccurrenceSpecification referenced by after.

definitions.name: GeneralOrdering
descriptions: A GeneralOrdering represents a binary relation between two OccurrenceSpecifications, to describe that one OccurrenceSpecification must occur before the other in a valid trace. This mechanism provides the ability to define partial orders of OccurrenceSpecifications that may otherwise not have a specified order.

definitions.name: Interaction.not_contained
descriptions: An Interaction instance must not be contained within another Interaction instance.

definitions.name: Interaction.action
descriptions: Actions owned by the Interaction.

definitions.name: Interaction.formalGate
descriptions: Specifies the gates that form the message interface between this Interaction and any InteractionUses which reference it.

definitions.name: Interaction.fragment
descriptions: The ordered set of fragments in the Interaction.

definitions.name: Interaction.lifeline
descriptions: Specifies the participants in this Interaction.

definitions.name: Interaction.message
descriptions: The Messages contained in this Interaction.

definitions.name: Interaction
descriptions: An Interaction is a unit of Behavior that focuses on the observable exchange of information between connectable elements.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.minint_maxint
descriptions: Minint/maxint can only be present if the InteractionConstraint is associated with the operand of a loop CombinedFragment.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.minint_non_negative
descriptions: If minint is specified, then the expression must evaluate to a non-negative integer.
definitions.limitation: Represented Integer values are checked. Unknown numeric expressions require an evaluator and remain unsupported; wrong computable literal kinds remain invalid.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.maxint_positive
descriptions: If maxint is specified, then the expression must evaluate to a positive integer.
definitions.limitation: Represented Integer values are checked. Unknown numeric expressions require an evaluator and remain unsupported; wrong computable literal kinds remain invalid.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.dynamic_variables
descriptions: The dynamic variables that take part in the constraint must be owned by the ConnectableElement corresponding to the covered Lifeline.
definitions.limitation: Trusted reference facts are checked against represented covered lifeline roles/types, interaction parameters/context attributes and read-only Properties. Full runtime ownership/global/write-once semantics remains a project approximation.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.global_data
descriptions: The constraint may contain references to global data or write-once data.
definitions.limitation: Trusted reference facts and represented read-only Properties are supported. Arbitrary domain global/write-once storage semantics is not represented by core UML and is not proved.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.maxint_greater_equal_minint
descriptions: If maxint is specified, then minint must be specified and the evaluation of maxint must be >= the evaluation of minint.
definitions.limitation: Represented Integer bounds are compared. Unknown numeric expressions require an evaluator and remain unsupported.

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.maxint
descriptions: The maximum number of iterations of a loop

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint.minint
descriptions: The minimum number of iterations of a loop

definitions.name: InteractionConstraint
descriptions: An InteractionConstraint is a Boolean expression that guards an operand in a CombinedFragment.

definitions.name: InteractionFragment.covered
descriptions: References the Lifelines that the InteractionFragment involves.

definitions.name: InteractionFragment.enclosingInteraction
descriptions: The Interaction enclosing this InteractionFragment.

definitions.name: InteractionFragment.enclosingOperand
descriptions: The operand enclosing this InteractionFragment (they may nest recursively).

definitions.name: InteractionFragment.generalOrdering
descriptions: The general ordering relationships contained in this fragment.

definitions.name: InteractionFragment
descriptions: InteractionFragment is an abstract notion of the most general interaction unit. An InteractionFragment is a piece of an Interaction. Each InteractionFragment is conceptually like an Interaction by itself.

definitions.name: InteractionOperand.guard_contain_references
descriptions: The guard must contain only references to values local to the Lifeline on which it resides, or values global to the whole Interaction.
definitions.limitation: Trusted guard reference facts are checked against represented operand coverage/context. General domain-global and write-once facts remain incomplete.

definitions.name: InteractionOperand.guard_directly_prior
descriptions: The guard must be placed directly prior to (above) the OccurrenceSpecification that will become the first OccurrenceSpecification within this InteractionOperand.
definitions.limitation: Guard composite ownership is checked. Graphical placement immediately above a fragment requires UMLDI/layout semantics and is not proved.

definitions.name: InteractionOperand.fragment
descriptions: The fragments of the operand.

definitions.name: InteractionOperand.guard
descriptions: Constraint of the operand.

definitions.name: InteractionOperand
descriptions: An InteractionOperand is contained in a CombinedFragment. An InteractionOperand represents one operand of the expression given by the enclosing CombinedFragment.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.gates_match
descriptions: Actual Gates of the InteractionUse must match Formal Gates of the referred Interaction. Gates match when their names are equal and their messages correspond.

expressions.body:
actualGate->notEmpty() implies 
refersTo.formalGate->forAll( fg : Gate | self.actualGate->select(matches(fg))->size()=1) and
self.actualGate->forAll(ag : Gate | refersTo.formalGate->select(matches(ag))->size()=1)

definitions.name: InteractionUse.arguments_are_constants
descriptions: The arguments must only be constants, parameters of the enclosing Interaction or attributes of the classifier owning the enclosing Interaction.
definitions.limitation: Foreign expression constancy/references require trusted analyzer facts; no arbitrary language execution is supplied.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.returnValueRecipient_coverage
descriptions: The returnValueRecipient must be a Property of a ConnectableElement that is represented by a Lifeline covered by this InteractionUse.

expressions.body:
returnValueRecipient->asSet()->notEmpty() implies
let covCE : Set(ConnectableElement) = covered.represents->asSet() in 
covCE->notEmpty() and let classes:Set(Classifier) = covCE.type.oclIsKindOf(Classifier).oclAsType(Classifier)->asSet() in 
let allProps : Set(Property) = classes.attribute->union(classes.allParents().attribute)->asSet() in 
allProps->includes(returnValueRecipient)

definitions.name: InteractionUse.arguments_correspond_to_parameters
descriptions: The arguments of the InteractionUse must correspond to parameters of the referred Interaction.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.returnValue_type_recipient_correspondence
descriptions: The type of the returnValue must correspond to the type of the returnValueRecipient.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.all_lifelines
descriptions: The InteractionUse must cover all Lifelines of the enclosing Interaction that are common with the lifelines covered by the referred Interaction. Lifelines are common if they have the same selector and represents associationEnd values.

expressions.body:
let parentInteraction : Set(Interaction) = enclosingInteraction->asSet()->
union(enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->closure(enclosingOperand.combinedFragment)->
collect(enclosingInteraction).oclAsType(Interaction)->asSet()) in
parentInteraction->size()=1 and let refInteraction : Interaction = refersTo in
parentInteraction.covered-> forAll(intLifeline : Lifeline | refInteraction.covered->
forAll( refLifeline : Lifeline | refLifeline.represents = intLifeline.represents and 
(
( refLifeline.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) implies
  intLifeline.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) and 
  refLifeline.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value = intLifeline.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value ) and
( refLifeline.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) implies
  intLifeline.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) and 
  refLifeline.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value = intLifeline.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value )
)
 implies self.covered->asSet()->includes(intLifeline)))

definitions.name: InteractionUse.actualGate
descriptions: The actual gates of the InteractionUse.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.argument
descriptions: The actual arguments of the Interaction.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.refersTo
descriptions: Refers to the Interaction that defines its meaning.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.returnValue
descriptions: The value of the executed Interaction.

definitions.name: InteractionUse.returnValueRecipient
descriptions: The recipient of the return value.

definitions.name: InteractionUse
descriptions: An InteractionUse refers to an Interaction. The InteractionUse is a shorthand for copying the contents of the referenced Interaction where the InteractionUse is. To be accurate the copying must take into account substituting parameters with arguments and connect the formal Gates with the actual ones.

definitions.name: Lifeline.selector_specified
descriptions: The selector for a Lifeline must only be specified if the referenced Part is multivalued.

definitions.name: Lifeline.interaction_uses_share_lifeline
descriptions: If a lifeline is in an Interaction referred to by an InteractionUse in an enclosing Interaction,  and that lifeline is common with another lifeline in an Interaction referred to by another InteractonUse within that same enclosing Interaction, it must be common to a lifeline within that enclosing Interaction. By common Lifelines we mean Lifelines with the same selector and represents associations.

expressions.body:
let intUses : Set(InteractionUse) = interaction.interactionUse  in 
intUses->forAll
( iuse : InteractionUse | 
let usingInteraction : Set(Interaction)  = iuse.enclosingInteraction->asSet()
->union(
iuse.enclosingOperand.combinedFragment->asSet()->closure(enclosingOperand.combinedFragment).enclosingInteraction->asSet()
               ) 
in
let peerUses : Set(InteractionUse) = usingInteraction.fragment->select(oclIsKindOf(InteractionUse)).oclAsType(InteractionUse)->asSet()
->union(
usingInteraction.fragment->select(oclIsKindOf(CombinedFragment)).oclAsType(CombinedFragment)->asSet()
->closure(operand.fragment->select(oclIsKindOf(CombinedFragment)).oclAsType(CombinedFragment)).operand.fragment->
select(oclIsKindOf(InteractionUse)).oclAsType(InteractionUse)->asSet()
               )->excluding(iuse)
 in
peerUses->forAll( peerUse : InteractionUse |
 peerUse.refersTo.lifeline->forAll( l : Lifeline | (l.represents = self.represents and 
 ( self.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) implies
  l.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) and 
  self.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value = l.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value )
  and 
( self.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) implies
  l.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) and 
  self.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value = l.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value )
)  
implies
 usingInteraction.lifeline->select(represents = self.represents and
 ( self.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) implies
  l.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralString) and 
  self.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value = l.selector.oclAsType(LiteralString).value )
and 
( self.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) implies
  l.selector.oclIsKindOf(LiteralInteger) and 
  self.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value = l.selector.oclAsType(LiteralInteger).value )
)
                                                )
                    )
)

definitions.name: Lifeline.same_classifier
descriptions: The classifier containing the referenced ConnectableElement must be the same classifier, or an ancestor, of the classifier that contains the interaction enclosing this lifeline.

definitions.name: Lifeline.selector_int_or_string
descriptions: The selector value, if present, must be a LiteralString or a LiteralInteger

definitions.name: Lifeline.coveredBy
descriptions: References the InteractionFragments in which this Lifeline takes part.

definitions.name: Lifeline.decomposedAs
descriptions: References the Interaction that represents the decomposition.

definitions.name: Lifeline.interaction
descriptions: References the Interaction enclosing this Lifeline.

definitions.name: Lifeline.represents
descriptions: References the ConnectableElement within the classifier that contains the enclosing interaction.

definitions.name: Lifeline.selector
descriptions: If the referenced ConnectableElement is multivalued, then this specifies the specific individual part within that set.

definitions.name: Lifeline
descriptions: A Lifeline represents an individual participant in the Interaction. While parts and structural features may have multiplicity greater than 1, Lifelines represent only one interacting entity.

definitions.name: Message.messageKind
descriptions: This query returns the MessageKind value for this Message.
definitions.limitation: The source body recursively returns the property itself. Python derives complete/lost/found/unknown from represented send and receive ends.

definitions.name: Message.isDistinguishableFrom
descriptions: The query isDistinguishableFrom() specifies that any two Messages may coexist in the same Namespace, regardless of their names.

definitions.name: Message.sending_receiving_message_event
descriptions: If the sendEvent and the receiveEvent of the same Message are on the same Lifeline, the sendEvent must be ordered before the receiveEvent.

expressions.body:
receiveEvent.oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)
implies
let f :  Lifeline = sendEvent->select(oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)).oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)->asOrderedSet()->first().covered in
f = receiveEvent->select(oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)).oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)->asOrderedSet()->first().covered  implies
f.events->indexOf(sendEvent.oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)->asOrderedSet()->first() ) < 
f.events->indexOf(receiveEvent.oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)->asOrderedSet()->first() )

definitions.limitation: The check uses represented ordered fragment containment with nested fragments visited before following siblings. A full partial-order semantics for parallel/alternative operands and GeneralOrdering is not implemented.

definitions.name: Message.arguments
descriptions: Arguments of a Message must only be: i) attributes of the sending lifeline, ii) constants, iii) symbolic values (which are wildcard values representing any legal value), iv) explicit parameters of the enclosing Interaction, v) attributes of the class owning the Interaction.
definitions.limitation: Constants and represented wildcard values are checked. Foreign expression constancy/references require trusted analyzer facts.

definitions.name: Message.cannot_cross_boundaries
descriptions: Messages cannot cross boundaries of CombinedFragments or their operands.  This is true if and only if both MessageEnds are enclosed within the same InteractionFragment (i.e., an InteractionOperand or an Interaction).

expressions.body:
sendEvent->notEmpty() and receiveEvent->notEmpty() implies
let sendEnclosingFrag : Set(InteractionFragment) = 
sendEvent->asOrderedSet()->first().enclosingFragment()
in 
let receiveEnclosingFrag : Set(InteractionFragment) = 
receiveEvent->asOrderedSet()->first().enclosingFragment()
in  sendEnclosingFrag = receiveEnclosingFrag

definitions.name: Message.signature_is_signal
descriptions: In the case when the Message signature is a Signal, the arguments of the Message must correspond to the attributes of the Signal. A Message Argument corresponds to a Signal Attribute if the Argument is of the same Class or a specialization of that of the Attribute.

expressions.body:
(messageSort = MessageSort::asynchSignal ) and signature.oclIsKindOf(Signal) implies
   let signalAttributes : OrderedSet(Property) = signature.oclAsType(Signal).inheritedMember()->
             select(n:NamedElement | n.oclIsTypeOf(Property))->collect(oclAsType(Property))->asOrderedSet()
   in signalAttributes->size() = self.argument->size()
   and self.argument->forAll( o: ValueSpecification |
          not (o.oclIsKindOf(Expression)
          and o.oclAsType(Expression).symbol->size()=0
          and o.oclAsType(Expression).operand->isEmpty() ) implies
              let p : Property = signalAttributes->at(self.argument->indexOf(o))
              in o.type.oclAsType(Classifier).conformsTo(p.type.oclAsType(Classifier)))

definitions.limitation: The source selects inheritedMember only. Python matches allAttributes including owned attributes according to the signal-signature description.

definitions.name: Message.occurrence_specifications
descriptions: If the MessageEnds are both OccurrenceSpecifications, then the connector must go between the Parts represented by the Lifelines of the two MessageEnds.

definitions.name: Message.signature_refer_to
descriptions: The signature must either refer an Operation (in which case messageSort is either synchCall or asynchCall or reply) or a Signal (in which case messageSort is asynchSignal). The name of the NamedElement referenced by signature must be the same as that of the Message.

definitions.name: Message.signature_is_operation_request
descriptions: In the case when a Message with messageSort synchCall or asynchCall has a non empty Operation signature, the arguments of the Message must correspond to the in and inout parameters of the Operation. A Parameter corresponds to an Argument if the Argument is of the same Class or a specialization of that of the Parameter.

expressions.body:
(messageSort = MessageSort::asynchCall or messageSort = MessageSort::synchCall) and signature.oclIsKindOf(Operation)  implies 
 let requestParms : OrderedSet(Parameter) = signature.oclAsType(Operation).ownedParameter->
 select(direction = ParameterDirectionKind::inout or direction = ParameterDirectionKind::_'in'  )
in requestParms->size() = self.argument->size() and
self.argument->forAll( o: ValueSpecification | 
not (o.oclIsKindOf(Expression) and o.oclAsType(Expression).symbol->size()=0 and o.oclAsType(Expression).operand->isEmpty() ) implies 
let p : Parameter = requestParms->at(self.argument->indexOf(o)) in
o.type.oclAsType(Classifier).conformsTo(p.type.oclAsType(Classifier))
)

definitions.name: Message.signature_is_operation_reply
descriptions: In the case when a Message with messageSort reply has a non empty Operation signature, the arguments of the Message must correspond to the out, inout, and return parameters of the Operation. A Parameter corresponds to an Argument if the Argument is of the same Class or a specialization of that of the Parameter.

expressions.body:
(messageSort = MessageSort::reply) and signature.oclIsKindOf(Operation) implies 
 let replyParms : OrderedSet(Parameter) = signature.oclAsType(Operation).ownedParameter->
select(direction = ParameterDirectionKind::inout or direction = ParameterDirectionKind::out or direction = ParameterDirectionKind::return)
in replyParms->size() = self.argument->size() and
self.argument->forAll( o: ValueSpecification | o.oclIsKindOf(Expression) and let e : Expression = o.oclAsType(Expression) in
e.operand->notEmpty()  implies 
let p : Parameter = replyParms->at(self.argument->indexOf(o)) in
e.operand->asSequence()->first().type.oclAsType(Classifier).conformsTo(p.type.oclAsType(Classifier))
)

definitions.limitation: The XMI predicate is preserved, including vacuous direct values. validate() additionally enforces prose:Message.reply_argument_types on direct typed values, first expression operands and wildcards; arbitrary expression evaluation remains outside this check.

definitions.name: MessageEnd.enclosingFragment
descriptions: This query returns a set including the enclosing InteractionFragment this MessageEnd is enclosed within.

expressions.body:
result = (if self->select(oclIsKindOf(Gate))->notEmpty() 
then -- it is a Gate
let endGate : Gate = 
  self->select(oclIsKindOf(Gate)).oclAsType(Gate)->asOrderedSet()->first()
  in
  if endGate.isOutsideCF() 
  then endGate.combinedFragment.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(endGate.combinedFragment.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet())
  else if endGate.isInsideCF() 
    then endGate.combinedFragment.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()
    else if endGate.isFormal() 
      then endGate.interaction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()
      else if endGate.isActual() 
        then endGate.interactionUse.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()->
     union(endGate.interactionUse.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet())
        else null
        endif
      endif
    endif
  endif
else -- it is a MessageOccurrenceSpecification
let endMOS : MessageOccurrenceSpecification  = 
  self->select(oclIsKindOf(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)).oclAsType(MessageOccurrenceSpecification)->asOrderedSet()->first() 
  in
  if endMOS.enclosingInteraction->notEmpty() 
  then endMOS.enclosingInteraction.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()
  else endMOS.enclosingOperand.oclAsType(InteractionFragment)->asSet()
  endif
endif)

definitions.limitation: The source returns null for an unclassified Gate. Python returns an empty collection matching the result signature.

definitions.name: MessageEnd.message
descriptions: References a Message.

definitions.name: MessageEnd
descriptions: MessageEnd is an abstract specialization of NamedElement that represents what can occur at the end of a Message.

definitions.name: MessageOccurrenceSpecification
descriptions: A MessageOccurrenceSpecification specifies the occurrence of Message events, such as sending and receiving of Signals or invoking or receiving of Operation calls. A MessageOccurrenceSpecification is a kind of MessageEnd. Messages are generated either by synchronous Operation calls or asynchronous Signal sends. They are received by the execution of corresponding AcceptEventActions.

definitions.name: OccurrenceSpecification.covered
descriptions: References the Lifeline on which the OccurrenceSpecification appears.

definitions.name: OccurrenceSpecification.toAfter
descriptions: References the GeneralOrderings that specify EventOcurrences that must occur after this OccurrenceSpecification.

definitions.name: OccurrenceSpecification.toBefore
descriptions: References the GeneralOrderings that specify EventOcurrences that must occur before this OccurrenceSpecification.

definitions.name: OccurrenceSpecification
descriptions: An OccurrenceSpecification is the basic semantic unit of Interactions. The sequences of occurrences specified by them are the meanings of Interactions.

definitions.name: PartDecomposition.commutativity_of_decomposition
descriptions: Assume that within Interaction X, Lifeline L is of class C and decomposed to D. Assume also that there is within X an InteractionUse (say) U that covers L. According to the constraint above U will have a counterpart CU within D. Within the Interaction referenced by U, L should also be decomposed, and the decomposition should reference CU. (This rule is called commutativity of decomposition.)

definitions.name: PartDecomposition.assume
descriptions: Assume that within Interaction X, Lifeline L is of class C and decomposed to D. Within X there is a sequence of constructs along L (such constructs are CombinedFragments, InteractionUse and (plain) OccurrenceSpecifications). Then a corresponding sequence of constructs must appear within D, matched one-to-one in the same order. i) CombinedFragment covering L are matched with an extra-global CombinedFragment in D. ii) An InteractionUse covering L is matched with a global (i.e., covering all Lifelines) InteractionUse in D. iii) A plain OccurrenceSpecification on L is considered an actualGate that must be matched by a formalGate of D.

definitions.name: PartDecomposition.parts_of_internal_structures
descriptions: PartDecompositions apply only to Parts that are Parts of Internal Structures not to Parts of Collaborations.

definitions.name: PartDecomposition
descriptions: A PartDecomposition is a description of the internal Interactions of one Lifeline relative to an Interaction.

definitions.name: StateInvariant.covered

definitions.name: StateInvariant.invariant
descriptions: A Constraint that should hold at runtime for this StateInvariant.

definitions.name: StateInvariant
descriptions: A StateInvariant is a runtime constraint on the participants of the Interaction. It may be used to specify a variety of different kinds of Constraints, such as values of Attributes or Variables, internal or external States, and so on. A StateInvariant is an InteractionFragment and it is placed on a Lifeline.

definitions.name: InformationFlow.must_conform
descriptions: The sources and targets of the information flow must conform to the sources and targets or conversely the targets and sources of the realization relationships.
definitions.limitation: Nominal endpoint conformance, distinct undirected channel sides and directed activity/message channels are checked as a project interpretation of the prose-only rule. Gate endpoints require explicit mappings; external lost/found endpoints remain unsupported. Runtime delivery is not proved.

definitions.name: InformationFlow.sources_and_targets_kind
descriptions:
The sources and targets of the information flow can only be one of the following kind: Actor, Node, UseCase, Artifact, Class, Component, Port, Property, Interface, Package, ActivityNode, ActivityPartition,
Behavior and InstanceSpecification except when its classifier is a relationship (i.e. it represents a link).

expressions.body:
(self.informationSource->forAll( sis |
  oclIsKindOf(Actor) or oclIsKindOf(Node) or oclIsKindOf(UseCase) or oclIsKindOf(Artifact) or 
  oclIsKindOf(Class) or oclIsKindOf(Component) or oclIsKindOf(Port) or oclIsKindOf(Property) or 
  oclIsKindOf(Interface) or oclIsKindOf(Package) or oclIsKindOf(ActivityNode) or oclIsKindOf(ActivityPartition) or 
  (oclIsKindOf(InstanceSpecification) and not sis.oclAsType(InstanceSpecification).classifier->exists(oclIsKindOf(Relationship))))) 

and

(self.informationTarget->forAll( sit | 
  oclIsKindOf(Actor) or oclIsKindOf(Node) or oclIsKindOf(UseCase) or oclIsKindOf(Artifact) or 
  oclIsKindOf(Class) or oclIsKindOf(Component) or oclIsKindOf(Port) or oclIsKindOf(Property) or 
  oclIsKindOf(Interface) or oclIsKindOf(Package) or oclIsKindOf(ActivityNode) or oclIsKindOf(ActivityPartition) or 
(oclIsKindOf(InstanceSpecification) and not sit.oclAsType(InstanceSpecification).classifier->exists(oclIsKindOf(Relationship)))))

definitions.limitation: The unqualified kind tests in the source refer to the flow instead of the endpoint. Python tests each endpoint and excludes InstanceSpecifications classified by Relationships.

definitions.name: InformationFlow.convey_classifiers
descriptions: An information flow can only convey classifiers that are allowed to represent an information item.

expressions.body:
self.conveyed->forAll(oclIsKindOf(Class) or oclIsKindOf(Interface)
  or oclIsKindOf(InformationItem) or oclIsKindOf(Signal) or oclIsKindOf(Component))

definitions.name: InformationFlow.conveyed
descriptions: Specifies the information items that may circulate on this information flow.

definitions.name: InformationFlow.informationSource
descriptions: Defines from which source the conveyed InformationItems are initiated.

definitions.name: InformationFlow
descriptions: InformationFlows describe circulation of information through a system in a general manner. They do not specify the nature of the information, mechanisms by which it is conveyed, sequences of exchange or any control conditions. During more detailed modeling, representation and realization links may be added to specify which model elements implement an InformationFlow and to show how information is conveyed.  InformationFlows require some kind of “information channel” for unidirectional transmission of information items from sources to targets.  They specify the information channel’s realizations, if any, and identify the information that flows along them.  Information moving along the information channel may be represented by abstract InformationItems and by concrete Classifiers.

definitions.name: InformationItem.sources_and_targets
descriptions: The sources and targets of an information item (its related information flows) must designate subsets of the sources and targets of the representation information item, if any. The Classifiers that can realize an information item can only be of the following kind: Class, Interface, InformationItem, Signal, Component.

expressions.body:
(self.represented->select(oclIsKindOf(InformationItem))->forAll(p |
  p.conveyingFlow.source->forAll(q | self.conveyingFlow.source->includes(q)) and
    p.conveyingFlow.target->forAll(q | self.conveyingFlow.target->includes(q)))) and
      (self.represented->forAll(oclIsKindOf(Class) or oclIsKindOf(Interface) or
        oclIsKindOf(InformationItem) or oclIsKindOf(Signal) or oclIsKindOf(Component)))

definitions.limitation: Python preserves the source direction: flows conveying a represented InformationItem must use subsets of the sources/targets of flows conveying self. The representation wording in the description is ambiguous and remains a source interpretation to resolve.

definitions.name: InformationItem.has_no
descriptions: An informationItem has no feature, no generalization, and no associations.
definitions.limitation: The source checks features/generalizations but omits associations. Python also checks Association end types in the model extent according to the prose.

definitions.name: InformationItem.not_instantiable
descriptions: It is not instantiable.
definitions.limitation: The source checks isAbstract only. Python additionally rejects represented InstanceSpecifications classified by this item, according to the prose.

definitions.name: InformationItem.represented
descriptions: Determines the classifiers that will specify the structure and nature of the information. An information item represents all its represented classifiers.

definitions.name: InformationItem
descriptions: InformationItems represent many kinds of information that can flow from sources to targets in very abstract ways.  They represent the kinds of information that may move within a system, but do not elaborate details of the transferred information.  Details of transferred information are the province of other Classifiers that may ultimately define InformationItems.  Consequently, InformationItems cannot be instantiated and do not themselves have features, generalizations, or associations. An important use of InformationItems is to represent information during early design stages, possibly before the detailed modeling decisions that will ultimately define them have been made. Another purpose of InformationItems is to abstract portions of complex models in less precise, but perhaps more general and communicable, ways.

definitions.name: Artifact.fileName
descriptions: A concrete name that is used to refer to the Artifact in a physical context. Example: file system name, universal resource locator.

definitions.name: Artifact.manifestation
descriptions: The set of model elements that are manifested in the Artifact. That is, these model elements are utilized in the construction (or generation) of the artifact.

definitions.name: Artifact.nestedArtifact
descriptions: The Artifacts that are defined (nested) within the Artifact. The association is a specialization of the ownedMember association from Namespace to NamedElement.

definitions.name: Artifact.ownedAttribute
descriptions: The attributes or association ends defined for the Artifact. The association is a specialization of the ownedMember association.

definitions.name: Artifact.ownedOperation
descriptions: The Operations defined for the Artifact. The association is a specialization of the ownedMember association.

definitions.name: Artifact
descriptions:
An artifact is the specification of a physical piece of information that is used or produced by a software development process, or by deployment and operation of a system. Examples of artifacts include model files, source files, scripts, and binary executable files, a table in a database system, a development deliverable, or a word-processing document, a mail message.
An artifact is the source of a deployment to a node.

definitions.name: CommunicationPath.association_ends
descriptions: The association ends of a CommunicationPath are typed by DeploymentTargets.

definitions.name: CommunicationPath
descriptions: A communication path is an association between two deployment targets, through which they are able to exchange signals and messages.

definitions.name: DeployedArtifact
descriptions: A deployed artifact is an artifact or artifact instance that has been deployed to a deployment target.

definitions.name: Deployment.configuration
descriptions: The specification of properties that parameterize the deployment and execution of one or more Artifacts.

definitions.name: Deployment.deployedArtifact
descriptions: The Artifacts that are deployed onto a Node. This association specializes the supplier association.

definitions.name: Deployment.location
descriptions: The DeployedTarget which is the target of a Deployment.

definitions.name: Deployment
descriptions:
A deployment is the allocation of an artifact or artifact instance to a deployment target.
A component deployment is the deployment of one or more artifacts or artifact instances to a deployment target, optionally parameterized by a deployment specification. Examples are executables and configuration files.

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification.deployment_target
descriptions: The DeploymentTarget of a DeploymentSpecification is a kind of ExecutionEnvironment.

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification.deployed_elements
descriptions: The deployedElements of a DeploymentTarget that are involved in a Deployment that has an associated Deployment-Specification is a kind of Component (i.e., the configured components).
definitions.limitation: The XMI predicate retains the Artifact-only derivation. validate() additionally checks prose:DeploymentSpecification.configured_instance_elements using modeled Artifact instances. Nested-artifact and runtime-copy semantics remain open.

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification.deployment
descriptions: The deployment with which the DeploymentSpecification is associated.

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification.deploymentLocation
descriptions: The location where an Artifact is deployed onto a Node. This is typically a 'directory' or 'memory address.'

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification.executionLocation
descriptions: The location where a component Artifact executes. This may be a local or remote location.

definitions.name: DeploymentSpecification
descriptions: A deployment specification specifies a set of properties that determine execution parameters of a component artifact that is deployed on a node. A deployment specification can be aimed at a specific type of container. An artifact that reifies or implements deployment specification properties is a deployment descriptor.

definitions.name: DeploymentTarget.deployedElement
descriptions: Derivation for DeploymentTarget::/deployedElement

definitions.name: DeploymentTarget.deployedElement
descriptions: The set of elements that are manifested in an Artifact that is involved in Deployment to a DeploymentTarget.
definitions.limitation: The XMI query retains its Artifact-only filter. The supplemental deployed_elements resolver expands direct manifestations of modeled Artifact classifiers/instances. Nested-artifact, inherited-manifestation, slot and runtime-copy semantics remain open.

definitions.name: DeploymentTarget.deployment
descriptions: The set of Deployments for a DeploymentTarget.

definitions.name: DeploymentTarget
descriptions: A deployment target is the location for a deployed artifact.

definitions.name: Device
descriptions: A device is a physical computational resource with processing capability upon which artifacts may be deployed for execution. Devices may be complex (i.e., they may consist of other devices).

definitions.name: ExecutionEnvironment
descriptions: An execution environment is a node that offers an execution environment for specific types of components that are deployed on it in the form of executable artifacts.

definitions.name: Manifestation.utilizedElement
descriptions: The model element that is utilized in the manifestation in an Artifact.

definitions.name: Manifestation
descriptions: A manifestation is the concrete physical rendering of one or more model elements by an artifact.

definitions.name: Node.internal_structure
descriptions: The internal structure of a Node (if defined) consists solely of parts of type Node.
definitions.limitation: The source tests Property parts as Node objects, which rejects every actual part. Python checks part.type according to the Node internal-structure description.

definitions.name: Node.nestedNode
descriptions: The Nodes that are defined (nested) within the Node.

definitions.name: Node
descriptions: A Node is computational resource upon which artifacts may be deployed for execution. Nodes can be interconnected through communication paths to define network structures.

definitions.name: Abstraction.mapping
descriptions: An OpaqueExpression that states the abstraction relationship between the supplier(s) and the client(s). In some cases, such as derivation, it is usually formal and unidirectional; in other cases, such as trace, it is usually informal and bidirectional. The mapping expression is optional and may be omitted if the precise relationship between the Elements is not specified.

definitions.name: Abstraction
descriptions: An Abstraction is a Relationship that relates two Elements or sets of Elements that represent the same concept at different levels of abstraction or from different viewpoints.

definitions.name: Comment.annotatedElement
descriptions: References the Element(s) being commented.

definitions.name: Comment.body
descriptions: Specifies a string that is the comment.

definitions.name: Comment
descriptions: A Comment is a textual annotation that can be attached to a set of Elements.

definitions.name: Constraint.boolean_value
descriptions: The ValueSpecification for a Constraint must evaluate to a Boolean value.

definitions.name: Constraint.no_side_effects
descriptions: Evaluating the ValueSpecification for a Constraint must not have side effects.
definitions.limitation: Foreign expressions require trusted analyzer facts or a declared static Boolean type; execution is not verified.

definitions.name: Constraint.not_apply_to_self
descriptions: A Constraint cannot be applied to itself.

definitions.name: Constraint.constrainedElement
descriptions: The ordered set of Elements referenced by this Constraint.

definitions.name: Constraint.context
descriptions: Specifies the Namespace that owns the Constraint.

definitions.name: Constraint.specification
descriptions: A condition that must be true when evaluated in order for the Constraint to be satisfied.

definitions.name: Constraint
descriptions: A Constraint is a condition or restriction expressed in natural language text or in a machine readable language for the purpose of declaring some of the semantics of an Element or set of Elements.

definitions.name: Dependency.client
descriptions: The Element(s) dependent on the supplier Element(s). In some cases (such as a trace Abstraction) the assignment of direction (that is, the designation of the client Element) is at the discretion of the modeler and is a stipulation.

definitions.name: Dependency.supplier
descriptions: The Element(s) on which the client Element(s) depend in some respect. The modeler may stipulate a sense of Dependency direction suitable for their domain.

definitions.name: Dependency
descriptions: A Dependency is a Relationship that signifies that a single model Element or a set of model Elements requires other model Elements for their specification or implementation. This means that the complete semantics of the client Element(s) are either semantically or structurally dependent on the definition of the supplier Element(s).

definitions.name: DirectedRelationship.source
descriptions: Specifies the source Element(s) of the DirectedRelationship.

definitions.name: DirectedRelationship.target
descriptions: Specifies the target Element(s) of the DirectedRelationship.

definitions.name: DirectedRelationship
descriptions: A DirectedRelationship represents a relationship between a collection of source model Elements and a collection of target model Elements.

definitions.name: Element.allOwnedElements
descriptions: The query allOwnedElements() gives all of the direct and indirect ownedElements of an Element.

definitions.name: Element.mustBeOwned
descriptions: The query mustBeOwned() indicates whether Elements of this type must have an owner. Subclasses of Element that do not require an owner must override this operation.

definitions.name: Element.has_owner
descriptions: Elements that must be owned must have an owner.

definitions.name: Element.not_own_self
descriptions: An element may not directly or indirectly own itself.

definitions.name: Element.ownedComment
descriptions: The Comments owned by this Element.

definitions.name: Element.ownedElement
descriptions: The Elements owned by this Element.

definitions.name: Element.owner
descriptions: The Element that owns this Element.

definitions.name: Element
descriptions: An Element is a constituent of a model. As such, it has the capability of owning other Elements.

definitions.name: ElementImport.imported_element_is_public

definitions.name: ElementImport.importedElement

definitions.name: ElementImport.importingNamespace
descriptions: Specifies the Namespace that imports a PackageableElement from another Namespace.

definitions.name: ElementImport.visibility
descriptions: Specifies the visibility of the imported PackageableElement within the importingNamespace, i.e., whether the  importedElement will in turn be visible to other Namespaces. If the ElementImport is public, the importedElement will be visible outside the importingNamespace while, if the ElementImport is private, it will not.

definitions.name: ElementImport
descriptions: An ElementImport identifies a NamedElement in a Namespace other than the one that owns that NamedElement and allows the NamedElement to be referenced using an unqualified name in the Namespace owning the ElementImport.
